BCS graduate students also are helping make sure the department is a welcoming, inclusive, and equitable community. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Center for Real Estate
Requirements: Required: Online application; Statement of objectives; Three letters of recommendation; Transcripts; English proficiency exam scores – international applicants only; CV or resume; Fellow Program and Fellowship Application Form. [1]
Department: School of Architecture and Planning, School of Engineering, Department of Economics, and the MIT Sloan School of Management
Fees: The MSRED tuition is a premium tuition, which means it is approximately 10% higher than the standard cost for other MIT graduate programs. [12]
Concentration: While there are no official concentration tracks in the MSRED program, students can complete a finance concentration by taking a specific suite of finance courses and completing a thesis on a financial topic. [11]
Description: Launched in 1983, the MSRED is the first one-year degree in real estate development and the most concentrated, science-based graduate degree in real estate available. Students benefit from CRE’s unique ecosystem of interconnected academic research and industry partnership allowing them to apply cutting-edge discoveries to practical problems in effective, equitable, and creative methods. MSRED students gain the critical tools and skills required to succeed in the rapidly evolving global real estate industry while also grounding their practice within the critical frameworks of social, economic, and environmental sustainability.
ScholarshipAmount: The MSRED program generally awards 2-3 Fellows annually. [12]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: Prospective student applications will be evaluated based on the following criteria: Understanding of the Chemical Engineering Fundamentals: The candidate's core knowledge of chemical kinetics, transport phenomena, thermodynamics, and the underlying quantitative skills that form the core solution methods for Chemical Engineers. Analytical and Scientific Preparation: A candidate's background in chemistry, biology, physics, mathematics, and computer science as relevant to the candidate's area(s) of interest. [6]
Description: The Master of Science in Chemical Engineering Practice (M.S.CEP) requires two semesters of graduate-level courses at MIT and one semester at the field stations of the Practice School, under photoshoot-direction of resident MIT staff. Credit for the Practice School semester is accepted in lieu of a Master's thesis. The courses at MIT comprise the required core curriculum, two additional required courses, and electives. This core curriculum is required of all chemical engineering graduate students irrespective of their degree objective. The electives, however, may be chosen from outside the Department to support particular interests. The degree requires that you complete: the core curriculum in chemical engineering; Courses in systems engineering and applied chemistry; Practice School requirements, including a one-semester industrial internship.  [2]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: Required for all applicants: Online application; Statement of Purpose; Three letters of recommendation; Transcripts; English proficiency exam scores – international applicants only. [2]
Concentration: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemical Engineering Practice (PhDCEP)
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy and Doctor of Science degrees in Chemical Engineering are identical; students may choose for themselves the appellation they prefer. [13] This traditional, research-based doctoral degree program provides a thorough grounding in the fundamental principles of chemical engineering, as well as an intensive research experience. [2, 13] The degree requires the completion of a core curriculum in chemical engineering, one chemical engineering H Level class, the departmental biology requirement, a minor program of related subjects outside of chemical engineering, written and oral doctoral qualifying examinations, and the writing and oral defense of a thesis on original research. [13] There is also a distinct program, the Doctor of Philosophy in Chemical Engineering Practice (Ph.D. CEP), which is a fixed-term, four-year program that includes coursework at the Sloan School of Management and is designed to prepare students for leadership positions in industry. [3, 7]
AverageScholarshipAmount: All Chemical Engineering graduate students in good standing are fully funded by the department. This includes full tuition, a stipend, and health insurance. [1]
ScholarshipAmount: In the 2024-2025 academic year, the stipend for PhD students is $4,445 per month. [1]
ScholarshipPercentage: 100% of tuition is covered for all PhD students in good standing. [1]
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, research assistantships, or teaching assistantships. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: A PDF copy of your college transcript(s) is required and can be uploaded to the application. This can be an unofficial transcript as official transcript(s) are only required if you are admitted into our program. For applicants whose primary language is not English, your TOEFL or IELTS scores are required. The MIT reporting code is 3514, and the department code is 62. Provide at 3 names and email addresses of people that can provide a letter of recommendation for you. You can provide more than 3 names, but not more than 5.
Fees.1: The tuition for a full-time graduate student for the 2024-2025 academic year is $61,990. [8, 9]
Description: The MIT Chemistry Department does not offer a terminal Master’s Degree Program. Students are admitted to the doctoral program only.
ScholarshipType: Research assistantships (RAs), Teaching assistantships (TAs), and Fellowships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemistry
Requirements: In addition to the completed online application, all applicants must submit the following: transcripts from all universities and colleges attended, 3-5 letters of recommendation, and a CV/resume. [2, 3, 4] Applicants are also asked to identify 3 faculty members they would be interested in working with. [2] For applicants whose primary language is not English, TOEFL or IELTS scores are required. [2, 3]
Concentration: ['Chemical Biology', 'Inorganic Chemistry', 'Materials', 'Organic Chemistry', 'Physical Chemistry', 'Theory']
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Chemistry at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology provides students with the opportunity to conduct research in several areas of chemistry. The graduate program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and academia.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Civil and Environmental Engineering
Requirements: Online application; Statement of Objectives that addresses experience and purpose as well as an example of technical work; Three letters of recommendation; Transcripts; English proficiency exam scores –international applicants only; CV or resume. [6]
Concentration: ['Environmental Chemistry', 'Environmental Fluid Mechanics', 'Ecology and Evolution', 'Hydrology and Hydroclimatology', 'Systems Engineering including Networks and Transportation', 'Materials, Structures and Geomechanics']
Description: The Master of Science (SM) is the research-focused graduate degree in the department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE). Each SM and PhD graduate student in our department is matched with one of our faculty members to work together on the research component of the graduate degree. Connecting graduate students through research interests with faculty and offering the opportunity for advanced course work is a combination that produces highly successful graduates that emerge as leaders in their fields. The Master of Science is not usually treated as a terminal degree but rather, a benchmark on the path to complete a PhD. In some cases, a terminal SM may be considered. [74]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Civil and Environmental Engineering
Description: Students are admitted to the PhD program following attainment of a Master of Science degree in civil and environmental engineering or in a related field. Doctoral studies consist of courses selected for the individual in consultation with a faculty guidance committee, successful completion of a preliminary and a qualifying examination, and an independent research culminating in a thesis. Each doctoral student must satisfy, through course work, a major within the department. In addition, 2 minor areas of course work appropriate for your area of research are required.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Computational and Systems Biology
Description: To provide education in this emerging field, the Computational and Systems Biology (CSB) program integrates MIT's world-renowned disciplines in biology, engineering, mathematics, and computer science. The program integrates biology, engineering, and computation to address complex problems in biological systems, and CSB PhD students have the opportunity to work with CSBi faculty from across the Institute. Graduates of the program are uniquely prepared to make novel discoveries, develop new methods, and establish new paradigms. They are also well-positioned to assume critical leadership roles in both academia and industry, where this field is becoming increasingly important. [1]
ScholarshipType: All CSB students are fully supported until they complete all the requirements of the PhD program. This support may come from sources such as a NIH T32 Training Grant; federally-sponsored fellowships from the NSF. [8]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Computational Science and Engineering
Department: MIT's College of Computing via the Center for Computational Science & Engineering (CCSE)
Concentration: ['Computational Modeling', 'Computational Concentration']
Description: The standalone doctoral program in Computational Science and Engineering (PhD in CSE) enables students to specialize at the doctoral level in fundamental, methodological aspects of computational science via focused coursework and a thesis. [4] The emphasis of thesis research activities is the development and analysis of broadly applicable computational approaches that advance the state of the art. [2, 4] Students are awarded the Doctor of Philosophy in Computational Science and Engineering upon successful completion of the program requirements and defense of a thesis describing significant contributions to the CSE field. [2, 4] Program requirements include a course of study comprising nine graduate subjects and a graduate seminar. [4] Core and concentration subjects cover six “ways of thinking” fundamental to CSE: discretization and numerical methods for partial differential equations; optimization methods; statistics and data-driven modeling; high-performance computing and/or algorithms; mathematical foundations (e.g., functional analysis, probability); modeling (i.e., a subject that treats mathematical modeling in any science or engineering discipline). [2] The interdisciplinary doctoral program in Computational Science and Engineering (PhD in CSE + Engineering or Science) offers students the opportunity to specialize at the doctoral level in a computation-related field of their choice via computationally-oriented coursework and a doctoral thesis with a disciplinary focus related to one of eight participating host departments, namely, Aeronautics and Astronautics; Chemical Engineering; Civil and Environmental Engineering; Earth, Atmospheric and Planetary Sciences; Materials Science and Engineering; Mathematics; Mechanical Engineering; or Nuclear Science and Engineering. [1, 4]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Data, Economics, and Design of Policy
Concentration: ['International Development Track', 'Public Policy Track']
Description: The fight against poverty and inequality is more data-driven than ever before. Producing and understanding rigorous evidence has become increasingly critical for those seeking to affect change globally, but opportunities to acquire these skills remain limited. As the first master's degree to be offered by MIT's Department of Economics, the Data, Economics, and Design of Policy (DEDP) program is designed to meet this rising demand. [1] Jointly run by the Economics Department and the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL), the program equips development professionals from across the globe with the practical skills and theoretical knowledge needed to tackle some of the world's most pressing challenges. [1] Our program draws students with a wide range of backgrounds. Whether they focus on policy, practice, or further academic study, our graduates go on to impactful careers in the development sector and government. [1] The DEDP program offers two tracks: The International Development Track allows learners to apply the tools acquired through the core courses to explore development issues that are most prevalent in low- and middle-income countries experiencing massive and persistent poverty. The Public Policy Track allows learners to build on the tools acquired through the core courses to address a range of public policies, including both local issues and those that transcend geographic boundaries. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences
Department: Department of Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences
Concentration: ['Earth and Planetary Sciences', 'Atmospheric Science', 'Climate Science']
Description: The Department of Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences offers the Master of Science degree. An individual program of study and research is arranged to suit the special background, needs, and goals of each student. [2] The program is worked out in detail by the student with his or her personal faculty advisor and a departmental committee. [2] The department offers opportunities for graduate study and research in a wide range of fields, including: Atmospheric chemistry, Atmospheric dynamics, Biogeochemistry, Climate chemistry, Climate dynamics, Computational earth, atmospheric, and planetary sciences, Geology, Geobiology, Geochemistry, Geophysics, Paleoclimate, and Planetary sciences. [3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences
Requirements: Required application components include an online application, a statement of objectives, three letters of recommendation, transcripts, and for international applicants, English proficiency exam scores. [12] The GRE General test is also required for the Fall 2026 admissions cycle. [12]
Fees.1: All students admitted to our doctoral programs are provided with full funding that includes a stipend, tuition, and health insurance. [3]
Concentration: ['Atmospheric chemistry', 'Atmospheric dynamics', 'Biogeochemistry', 'Climate chemistry', 'Climate dynamics', 'Computational earth, atmospheric, and planetary sciences', 'Geology', 'Geobiology', 'Geochemistry', 'Geophysics', 'Paleoclimate', 'Planetary sciences']
Description: With the assistance of their faculty advisor, each student follows an individualized program of study encompassing core subjects, basic science and mathematics, and subjects related to the student's area of interest. Faculty advisors may be members of the Department of Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences or other MIT departments. Students typically receive their degree in five years. The first two years are spent in coursework and research, culminating in a general examination, which must be completed before the end of the second year. Following the general examination, the student forms a thesis committee and presents a thesis proposal. The thesis committee includes the faculty advisor and at least three other faculty members. The student defends their thesis in a public defense. The thesis must meet high professional standards and make a significant original contribution to the student's chosen research area. [3]
ScholarshipAmount: All admitted doctoral students receive full funding, which includes a stipend, tuition, and health insurance. [3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Economics
Requirements: Your application is considered complete when you have successfully submitted the following requirements by the December 15 application deadline: Online application. $90 application fee. Scanned copy of college transcripts. Three letters of recommendation. Resume/CV. [3]
Fees: Full tuition coverage is provided for all admitted students for the duration of the program, contingent on satisfactory academic progress. [100]
Description: Year after year, our top-ranked PhD program sets the standard for graduate economics training across the country. [2] Graduate students work closely with our world-class faculty to develop their own research and prepare to make impactful contributions to the field. [2] Our doctoral program enrolls 20-24 full-time students each year and students complete their degree in five to six years. [2] Students undertake core coursework in microeconomic theory, macroeconomics, and econometrics, and are expected to complete two major and two minor fields in economics. [2]
ScholarshipAmount: All admitted PhD students are offered fellowship support that includes full tuition, a nine-month stipend, and health insurance. [100]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Requirements: The only absolute, institute-level requirement for admission as a regular graduate student at MIT is that an applicant must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution before enrolling. [2] Beyond this, application materials and specific requirements are determined by the individual departments. [8, 10] General application materials that *may* be required by departments include letters of recommendation, a statement of objectives, a CV/resume, transcripts, and potentially GRE scores. [2] Each department oversees its own application process, and requirements can vary significantly. [2]
Concentration: ['Electrical Engineering: Bioelectrical Engineering; Circuit Design and Systems; Electromagnetics, Energy and Power; Information and System Science; Materials and Devices; Photonics and Quantum Technology', 'Computer Science: Computer Architecture; Computer Networks; Computer Systems; Programming Languages; Human Computer Interaction; Theoretical Computer Science', 'Artificial Intelligence and Decision-making: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Life Sciences; Computer Graphics; Computer vision; Machine Learning; Natural Language and Speech Processing; Artificial Intelligence; Robotics']
Description: The department requires that the 66-unit program consist of at least four subjects from a list of approved subjects by the Graduate Office which must include a minimum of 42 units of advanced graduate subjects. In addition, a 24-unit thesis is required beyond the 66 units. Students working full-time for the Master of Science degree may take as many as four classroom subjects per term. The subjects are wholly elective and are not restricted to those given by the department. [2]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Requirements: Online application; Essay 1: Your research activities and goals; Essay 2: Your academic and intellectual journey; Three letters of recommendation; Transcripts; English proficiency exam scores. [3]
MinimumTOEFLScore: 100 for the Internet-based test, 250 for the computer-based test, and 600 on the paper-based test

ProgramName: Master of Science in Health Sciences and Technology
Department: Harvard-MIT Program in Health Sciences and Technology
Description: The HST Master's Degree is only an option for students withdrawing from an HST PhD program who would like a terminal SM. [10]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Health Sciences and Technology
Requirements: Applicants to the Medical Engineering and Medical Physics (MEMP) PhD program should have an undergraduate degree in an engineering discipline or a physical/quantitative science field (for example, chemistry, physics, computer science, computational neuroscience). [1] A master's degree is not required. [5] Successful candidates typically have a grade point average of 3.6 or higher on a 4.0 scale, strong letters of recommendation, and relevant prior research experience. [5] Three letters of recommendation are required. [5] The statement of purpose should address the rationale for training in MEMP, as opposed to a more traditional science or engineering PhD program. [1]
Concentration: The formal name of the PhD program is Medical Engineering and Medical Physics (MEMP). The program also offers optional training programs in Neuroimaging and Bioastronautics. [6]
Description: HST's Medical Engineering and Medical Physics (MEMP) PhD program offers a unique curriculum for engineers and scientists who want to impact patient care by developing innovations to prevent, diagnose, and treat disease. As a MEMP student, you'll choose one of 11 technical concentrations and design an individualized curriculum to ground yourself in the foundations of that discipline. You'll study medical sciences alongside MD students and become fluent in the language and culture of medicine through structured clinical experiences. You'll select a research project from among laboratories at MIT, Harvard, affiliated hospitals and research institutes, then tackle important questions through the multiple lenses of your technical discipline and your medical training. [1, 3] As a result, you will learn how to ask better questions, identify promising research areas, and translate research findings into real-world medical practice. [3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in History, Anthropology, and Science, Technology, and Society
Requirements: Due to the decentralized nature of graduate admissions at MIT, most application requirements are set by the individual departments and may vary. Applicants should consult the specific degree program's page for detailed requirements. [19] Applicants are permitted to apply to more than one department, but this requires submitting separate applications, paying separate fees, and meeting all requirements for each program. [19]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: Combining the disciplines of History, Anthropology, and Science, Technology, and Society, the HASTS program at MIT prepares students to do intensive research on topics of global relevance—leading to outcomes with global impact. [1] The HASTS program requirements prepare students with the breadth and depth of knowledge and skills needed to embark on their intensive dissertation research by the summer after their third year and—at the completion of the five- to six-year program—write a dissertation based on an original research project. [1] Students take three core classes in their first year, covering all the HASTS disciplines; the remaining seven classes for the 10-class requirement can be taken within the three disciplines, elsewhere at MIT, or through cross-registration at Harvard. [1] MIT's doctoral program in History, Anthropology, and Science, Technology and Society (HASTS) is widely recognized as one of the best of its type in the world. Co-sponsored by STS, the Anthropology Program, and the History Faculty, it is a flagship program in the humanities at MIT. [5] The educational philosophy of the program assumes that it is the responsibility of doctoral students to take the initiative to use the resources of HASTS, and of MIT more generally, to develop their own approach to STS studies. [5]

ProgramName: Master of Engineering in Advanced Manufacturing and Design
Requirements: Applications to the Mechanical Engineering (MechE) Graduate Program are accepted from persons who have completed, or will have completed by the time they arrive, a Bachelor's degree. Most incoming students will have a degree in mechanical engineering or ocean engineering. However, the department's admission criteria are not specific in this regard, and talented students with backgrounds in other branches of engineering or in science may apply. A completed application consists of: The completed application form, Statement of Objectives, a minimum of three letters of recommendation, and uploaded official/unofficial copies of transcripts. [1]
Description: The Master of Engineering in Advanced Manufacturing and Design (MEng) is a 12-month professional degree program from MIT's Department of Mechanical Engineering that prepares students for leadership positions in the manufacturing industries. [2, 4] The program curriculum includes subjects in manufacturing processes and process control, factory systems and supply chains, business fundamentals, and the product development process. [2] It combines in-depth, group-based graduate subjects and a project-based thesis experience at leading companies to accelerate students' engineering and leadership skills. [2, 4] There are two paths to this degree: a traditional 12-month, full-time residency program, and a blended program that allows learners who have completed the MITx MicroMasters program credential in Principles of Manufacturing to spend eight months in residence at MIT to fulfill the remaining requirements. [1]
ScholarshipType: Research Assistantships, Teaching Assistantships, and Fellowships

ProgramName: Master of Engineering in Advanced Manufacturing and Design - Integrated Photonics
Concentration: Integrated Photonics
Description: To qualify for this degree, a student must complete a highly integrated set of subjects and projects that cover the process, product, system, and business aspects of manufacturing, totaling 90 units, plus complete a group-based thesis project with a manufacturing industry. [10] While centered in engineering and rmly grounded in the engineering sciences, this degree program considers the entire enterprise of manufacturing. [10] The Master of Engineering in Advanced Manufacturing and Design is a 12-month professional degree in mechanical engineering that is intended to prepare the student to assume a role of technical leadership in the manufacturing industries. [8, 10] The degree is aimed at practitioners who will use this knowledge to become leaders in existing, as well emerging, manufacturing companies. [8, 10]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Building Technology
Description: The Master of Science in Building Technology (SMBT) is a research-oriented program designed for graduate students interested in the development and application of advanced technology in buildings. [1] The program accepts students with undergraduate degrees in a variety of engineering disciplines, in the physical sciences, or in architecture, with a suitable background in technology. [2] All share both a keen interest in buildings and a thorough education in mathematics, physics, and other technical subjects. [1] Students will be incorporated into active and ongoing research projects while pursuing their own intellectual and career agendas. [1] Areas of study are highly interdisciplinary and address topics at diverse scales, from individual building components to broader urban energy and material flows. [1] Each student works on research directly with a Building Technology faculty member. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemical Engineering Practice
Requirements: Required for all applicants: Online application; Statement of Purpose; Three letters of recommendation; Transcripts; English proficiency exam scores – international applicants only. [16]

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration
Concentration: ['Business Analytics Certificate', 'Product Management Certificate', 'Enterprise Management Certificate', 'Entrepreneurship & Innovation Certificate', 'Finance Certificate', 'Healthcare Certificate', 'Sustainability Certificate']
Description: The two-year, full-time MBA program provides the intellectual discovery and expert faculty you'd expect from MIT, combined with the flexibility to customize coursework to your goals. [2] Your MBA journey begins with a core semester, where you and your cohort build a strong foundation in leadership, economics, and data-driven decision-making. [2] After the first-semester core, you can choose your electives—and real-world learning opportunities—to ensure that you're prepared to analyze and act. [2]

ProgramName: Master of Finance
Requirements: The MIT Sloan Master of Finance (MFin) program seeks intelligent, motivated applicants who are passionate about finance. Recent graduates, as well as early-career professionals in finance, engineering, mathematics, physics, and computer programming, are encouraged to apply. Applicants are evaluated based on their academic and professional achievements.
Fees: $93,834 for 12 months and $128,820 for 18 months for the 2025-2026 academic year. [10]
Fees.1: $93,834 for 12 months and $128,820 for 18 months for the 2025-2026 academic year. [10]
Concentration: ['Capital Markets', 'Corporate Finance', 'Financial Engineering', 'Climate and Social Impact Finance', 'FinTech']
Description: The Master of Finance (MFin) program at MIT Sloan is a STEM-designated program tailored for early-career individuals who want to succeed in the finance industry. It features a customizable curriculum that offers a thorough and in-depth understanding of financial markets and systems. The program places a strong emphasis on quantitative and analytical skills, with rigorous coursework based on modern financial theories and practices. Through action learning opportunities like Proseminars and the Finance Lab, students tackle real-world financial problems, preparing them to apply their knowledge to intricate issues and take the lead in the dynamic global market.

ProgramName: Master of Business Analytics
ScholarshipType: MIT Sloan matriculates the most promising Master of Business Analytics candidates regardless of financial circumstances. Support typically includes personal savings, loans, fellowship/scholarship awards, government or employer sponsorship, or some combination of these.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Management Studies
Master of Business Administration in Executive
Description: The MIT EMBA is a transformational journey for leaders like you who want to redefine potential and lead with purpose. We teach the science of management at MIT Sloan, providing our EMBA students with an exceptional forum for innovation and leadership through applied learning projects. The MIT EMBA helps leaders grow in their careers in ways that might have once seemed impossible. This 20-month program offers something rare: the community, resources, and opportunity to redefine not just your career, but your life. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Sloan Fellows
Requirements: A complete application for the Sloan Fellows MBA program requires a Cover Letter, a one-page Resume, a 60-second video statement and a second video question, one Letter of Recommendation, two additional professional references, an Organizational Chart, Transcripts, and two professional short answer questions. [7] A minimum of ten years of full-time work experience is a prerequisite for applying. [4] The cover letter should be 300 words or less and addressed to the Admissions Committee, seeking a place in the program. [5] The letter of recommendation must be submitted by the recommender through the university's online portal. [4]
Description: The MIT Sloan Fellows MBA program is a 12-month, full-time, residential experience designed for mid-career leaders who are ready to drive change and make a global impact. Built on the pillars of leadership, innovation, and a global perspective, the program offers a unique opportunity to customize your experience with access to electives, industry projects, and independent research to tailor the curriculum to your professional goals. The program offers three degree options: an MBA, a Master of Science in Management, or a Master of Science in Management of Technology. Throughout the year, you'll engage in intensive sessions with an executive coach to refine your leadership strategy and embark on a transformative journey that prepares you to lead in a complex, global environment.
ScholarshipAmount: Up to $20,000 for the AIM Scholarship and $25,000 from the Yellow Ribbon Program for eligible veterans. [8]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based fellowships, Dean's Fellowships, Action, Impact & Motivation (AIM) Scholarship, Kennedy Memorial Trust Scholarship, and Yellow Ribbon GI Education Enhancement Program. [8]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Integrated Design and Management
Master of Science in System Design and Management
Requirements: To qualify for the SDM master's program, candidates must either: Hold a B.S. degree in engineering, science, or technology, and have five or more years of professional technical experience with increasing responsibility; or. Hold an M.S. degree in engineering, science, or technology, and have three or more years of professional experience in a technical field, including some leadership experience. [2] Required application components include an online application, a statement of objectives, three letters of recommendation, transcripts, English proficiency exam scores, and a CV or resume. [3]
Department: School of Engineering and Sloan School of Management
Description: The System Design & Management (SDM) Master's program offers early and mid-career professionals an innovative and customizable curriculum of advanced engineering and management skills. [2] Drawing on MIT's rigorous academics and real-time connections to industry, our fellows learn to use systems thinking to understand the technical, managerial, and societal components of large-scale, complex challenges. [2] The multidisciplinary program allows fellows to see the world and relationships in new ways. [2, 6] Through rigorous classroom assignments and projects, fellows gain an inclusive and holistic view and graduate ready to take on leadership roles. [2, 6] The SDM Master's program is composed of a core course sequence, paired with a customizable curriculum of depth, foundation, and elective courses. [2, 6] Working closely with the program's academic advisors, fellows are able to tailor the program to support individual professional goals, exploring MIT's vast range of academic offerings. [2, 6] The curriculum encompasses leadership development, critical, creative, and integrative thinking, as well as an appreciation of diversity and an understanding of how to foster positive change within organizations and society. [3, 10]

ProgramName: Master of Applied Science
Requirements: For the degree of Master of Applied Science with specification of the field in which the student has specialized, the student must have completed satisfactorily at least 90 units of credit (including at least 66 units of graduate subject credit) from within a program of study that includes a slate of required and elective courses, and a capstone experience, both acceptable to the department in which the student is enrolled. [7] The candidate must also have been in residence for a minimum of one regular term. [7]
Concentration: ['Data, Economics, and Design of Policy', 'Music Technology and Computation']
Description: For the degree of Master of Applied Science with specification of the field in which the student has specialized, the student must have completed satisfactorily at least 90 units of credit (including at least 66 units of graduate subject credit) from within a program of study that includes a slate of required and elective courses, and a capstone experience, both acceptable to the department in which the student is enrolled. The candidate must also have been in residence for a minimum of one regular term. [3]

ProgramName: Master in City Planning
Requirements: Required for all applicants: Online application; Statement of objectives; Three letters of recommendation; Transcripts; English proficiency exam scores – international applicants only; CV or Resume. [3]
Fees.1: $64,310 per full-time academic year for both in-state and out-of-state residents for the 2025-2026 academic year. [2]
Concentration: ['city design and development', 'environmental policy and planning', 'housing, community, and economic development', 'international development', 'urban science', 'mobility']
Description: DUSP provides graduate professional education for individuals who will assume planning roles in public, private, and nonprofit agencies, firms, and international institutions, in the United States and abroad. [3] The Master in City Planning (MCP) is a professional degree in the field of planning and seeks to provide MCP students with the skills and specialized knowledge needed to fill traditional and emerging planning roles. [3] The two-year MCP program emphasizes the mastery of the tools necessary for effective practice, and is therefore distinct from liberal arts programs in urban affairs. [3] An intensive course of study stresses skills for policy analysis and institutional intervention. [3] MCP graduates work in a broad array of roles, from traditional city planning to economic, social, and environmental planning. [3]
Accredidation: The Master in City Planning program is accredited by the Planning Accreditation Board (PAB). [3]
ScholarshipPercentage: Approximately two-thirds of the MCP class receive some form of tuition assistance; of these, about half receive full-tuition awards for two years, while others are typically offered half-tuition grants. [18]
ScholarshipType: Tuition assistance, full-tuition awards, half-tuition grants, and research assistantships. [15, 18]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Political Science
Requirements: Application requirements include an online application, statement of objectives, personal statement, three letters of recommendation, transcripts, GRE scores, a CV or resume, and a writing sample. [4] For international applicants, English proficiency exam scores are also required. [4] The program requires the satisfactory completion of a minimum of six graduate subjects, at least 66 units of a program of study, and a minimum of three semesters. [2] A master's thesis is also required, and a GPA of 3.5 must be maintained. [2]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Political Science
Requirements:
Application Requirements:

Online application; Statement of objectives; Personal statement; Three letters of recommendation; Transcripts; English proficiency exam scores – international applicants only; GRE scores; CV or Resume; Writing sample. [2]
Concentration: ['American Politics', 'Comparative Politics', 'International Relations', 'Models and Methods', 'Political Economy', 'Security Studies']
Description: Our doctoral students are advancing political science as a discipline. They explore the empirical phenomena that produce new scholarly insights—insights that improve the way governments and societies function. As a result, MIT Political Science graduates are sought after for top teaching and research positions in the U.S. and abroad. The MIT PhD in Political Science requires preparation in two of these major fields. [2] You will need two full academic years of work to prepare for the general examinations and to meet other pre-dissertation requirements. Typically, a minimum of eight graduate subjects are required for a PhD. [2]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Linguistics
Requirements: The MIT application for the graduate program in linguistics includes a statement of purpose, an academic transcript from each college/university attended, three letters of recommendation, and a writing sample. GRE scores are not required. International applicants whose first language is not English may need to demonstrate English proficiency.
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: The graduate program in linguistics at MIT was set up to be a PhD program. Our students come from all over the world and from a wide range of academic backgrounds. We want to make sure that they all have a common foundation in the field of linguistics, and so the first two years are largely taken up with coursework. At the same time, from the very beginning, students are encouraged to pursue their own research interests. We have a very low student/faculty ratio, and our students work closely with faculty on independent research projects, starting as early as their first semester. After the first two years of coursework, students focus on their own research, which eventually results in a dissertation and a PhD. Many of our students also take classes at and work with faculty from other departments at MIT, and from other schools in the Boston area.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Linguistics
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Master of Science in Science Writing
Master of Science in Technology and Policy Program
Description: The Technology and Policy Program (TPP) prepares and educates leaders to address important technological issues confronting society. Through our two-year Master of Science Program, we prepare students for leadership in government and industry. Degree requirements include graduate-level coursework in engineering, policy, economics and law, and an interdisciplinary thesis focused on a technology policy issue.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: Applicants to MIT are not admitted to a specific major, but to the institute as a whole. All first-year students enter MIT without a declared major and explore their options during their first year before selecting a major. The application process is the same for all prospective first-year students. The application includes a series of short-answer essays and questions.
Concentration: Aerospace Information Technology
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering (Course 16) program is designed to prepare the graduate for an entry-level position in aerospace and related fields and for further education at the master's level. [14] The formal learning in the program builds a conceptual understanding in the foundational engineering sciences and professional subjects that span the topics critical to aerospace. [14] The program provides a foundation in the disciplines related to engineering aerospace vehicles and systems, including aerodynamics, fluid mechanics, propulsion, structural design and analysis, advanced materials, and dynamics. [5] Additional topics include feedback, control, estimation, control of flight vehicles, software engineering, human systems engineering, aerospace communications, autonomous systems, and digital systems. [5] The department's vision is to create an aerospace field that is a supportive community, pushing the boundaries of the possible to ensure a lasting positive impact on the nation, economy, and society. [14] It aims to educate the next generation of leaders, creative engineers, and entrepreneurs who will shape the future of aerospace. [14]
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Aerospace Engineering. [5, 13, 14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in American Studies
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Concentration: ['American literature', 'folklore and popular culture', 'black history and culture', "women's studies", 'American history, politics, or law', 'the history of science and technology', 'American art, architecture, or music']
Description: American Studies at MIT offers students the opportunity to organize subjects from various fields (e.g., history, anthropology, literature, political science, music, art, architecture, and urban planning) into personally constructed interdisciplinary programs as a way of gaining an integrated understanding of American society and culture. [1] Students can focus on any of several areas of interest, such as American literature; folklore and popular culture; black history and culture; women's studies; American history, politics, or law; the history of science and technology; and American art, architecture, or music. [1] A program in American Studies is ideal for preparing students for further work not only in the various humanistic fields, but also in law, urban planning, management, architecture, engineering, medicine, teaching, and the media. [1] The program has three primary objectives: to understand the underlying system of beliefs that informs every aspect of American culture—its myths, institutions, politics and literature, its characteristic dreams and rituals; to understand the uses and limits of different methods and intellectual disciplines as tools for exploring the complexities of a culture; and to understand the American present in relation to the American past. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Anthropology
Requirements: For undergraduate admissions, MIT requires the SAT or ACT. There are also other application components that are detailed on the admissions website. For graduate admissions, the only institute-level requirement is a bachelor's degree or its equivalent. Specific admission requirements vary significantly between departments and degree programs, and applicants are evaluated based on their prior performance and professional promise.
Description: The undergraduate program leading to the degree of Bachelor of Science in Anthropology (Course 21A) provides a thorough grounding in cultural anthropology. Majors learn about the concept of culture and the processes by which humans make meaningful transactions, the nature of ethnographic eldwork, a and the connections between anthropology and the other social sciences. Majors study the theories explaining human behavior as well as the range of methods anthropologists use to analyze empirical data. Students can focus on particular geographical areas, including Asia, Africa, Europe, Latin America, or North America, and on such issues as immigration, multiculturalism, environmental justice, medicine, globalization, religion, social media, cultures of computing, or food cultures. The anthropology student comes to understand that the hallmark of the discipline is the comparative study of human diversity.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Archaeology and Materials
Requirements: The application for first-year admission includes several components: a biographical information section, essays, a section to list your activities, academic transcripts from your school, a Secondary School Report, an application fee (or fee waiver), and two letters of recommendation (one from a math or science teacher, and one from a humanities, social science, or language teacher).
Department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
Concentration: Archaeology and Materials (Course 3-C)
Description: The 3C program is designed to afford students broad exposure to fields that contribute fundamental theoretical and methodological approaches to the study of ancient and historic, non-industrial societies. [1] The primary fields that comprise the curriculum include anthropological archaeology, geology, and materials science and engineering. [1] The 3C curriculum is structured to provide full balance between archaeology and archaeological science on one hand and materials science and engineering on the other. [1] The program's special focus is on understanding prehistoric societies through study of the materials technologies practiced by those societies. [1] Such study requires investigation into the structure and properties of materials associated with human activities. Investigating peoples' interactions with materials, the objects that those interactions produced, as well as the social and environmental settings that supported specific materials technologies leads to a fuller analysis of the physical, social, cultural, and ideological worlds in which people function. [1] Participation in laboratory work is an integral part of the curriculum. [1] The program requires that students take a materials laboratory course. [1] Some of the archaeology subjects are designed with a laboratory component. [1]
ScholarshipType: MIT offers scholarships based on financial need.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Art and Design
Requirements: Applicants apply to the university as a whole, not to a specific major. All first-year students begin as 'undeclared'. [17] General first-year application requirements include MIT's own online application, a $75 application fee (with waivers available), and submission of standardized test scores. [3, 4] While no specific high school classes are mandatory, applicants are expected to have a strong academic foundation from a rigorous program. [3] An interview with a member of the MIT Educational Council is also offered to applicants. [3]
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Art and Design (BSAD) provides undergraduates with a cohesive program of study that exposes them to cross-disciplinary fields in art and design. [12] It provides a rigorous conceptual foundation along with strong practical skills that can be applied across diverse design domains. [12] Students are introduced to the design process, from concept to completion, through contextual critical thinking, experimentation, representation, and physical production techniques, critique, iteration, and reflection. [12] The objective is to prepare students to pursue diverse career paths from product design to visual communication to information design to 2D and 3D art practices and more. [12] Study in this program will enable students to take advantage of emerging opportunities in industry and academia. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Asian and Asian Diaspora Studies
Requirements: Application requirements are not specific to this major, as applicants apply to MIT as a whole and enter undeclared. [13] General first-year application requirements include the online application (which contains biographical information, essays, and a list of activities), a Secondary School Report with an official high school transcript, two letters of recommendation (one from a math or science teacher and one from a humanities or language teacher), and SAT or ACT scores. [14, 2] An interview is also a component of the application process. [14]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: The Major in Asian and Asian Diaspora Studies is designed for students interested in serious intensive research on the languages, history, politics, and cultures of Asia and/or the Asian diasporas. The geographic region of Asia includes countries such as Bangladesh, China, India, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, Pakistan, the Philippines, Taiwan, and Vietnam. In consultation with the major advisor, students may focus their coursework on a sub-region of Asia, on one of the Asian diasporas, or design their program to offer a comparative study across different regions and/or cultural groups. The goal of the Major program is to provide balanced coverage of language, humanistic and social science offerings on the region and to expose students to some comparative perspectives within the region. [3, 5] All interdisciplinary major students must write a senior thesis on a topic of their choice to be determined in consultation with an MIT faculty member whose specialty falls within Asian studies. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biological Engineering
Requirements: Application requirements are not specific to the Bachelor of Science in Biological Engineering but apply to all undergraduate applicants to MIT. General requirements include the online application, two letters of recommendation (one from a math or science teacher and one from a humanities, social science, or language teacher), SAT or ACT scores, and a high school transcript. While not explicitly required, most competitive applicants have taken courses in calculus, physics, and chemistry.
Description: The Department of Biological Engineering offers an undergraduate curriculum that emphasizes quantitative, engineering-based analysis, design, and synthesis in the study of modern biology from the molecular to the systems level. The mission of the Department of Biological Engineering (BE) is to educate next-generation leaders and to generate and translate new knowledge in a new bioscience-based engineering discipline fusing engineering analysis and synthesis approaches with modern molecular-to-genomic biology. Combining quantitative, physical, and integrative principles with advances in mechanistic molecular and cellular bioscience, biological engineering increases understanding of how biological systems function as both physical and chemical mechanisms; how they respond when perturbed by factors such as medical therapeutics, environmental agents, and genetic variation; and how to manipulate and construct them toward beneficial use.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology
Requirements: When you apply to MIT, you apply to the entire university, not to a specific major or school. All first-year students begin at MIT as undeclared. [22] The general application requirements include the application form with essays and an activities section, two letters of recommendation (one from a math/science teacher and one from a humanities/social sciences/language teacher), a Secondary School Report with your transcript, and SAT or ACT scores. [5, 6, 7] An interview is also a part of the application process. [7]
Description: The curriculum leading to the Bachelor of Science in Biology is designed to prepare students for a professional career in the area of the biological sciences. [1, 2] Graduates of this program are well prepared for positions in industrial or research institutes. [1, 2] However, experience has shown that many graduates choose to continue their education at a graduate school in order to obtain a PhD in an area such as biochemistry, microbiology, genetics, biophysics, cell biology, or physiology, followed by research or teaching in one of those areas. [1] The undergraduate curriculum is also excellent preparation for students who wish to continue their education toward an MD, particularly if their career plans include laboratory investigations bearing on human disease. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Brain and Cognitive Sciences
Requirements: Application to the Bachelor of Science in Brain and Cognitive Sciences is handled through the general MIT undergraduate admissions process, as students do not declare a major until after their first year. General application components include the online MIT Application (which includes essays and an activities section), two letters of recommendation (one from a math/science teacher and one from a humanities/social science/language teacher), and a Secondary School Report with a high school transcript. [16] Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are also required. [7]
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Brain and Cognitive Sciences prepares students to pursue advanced degrees or careers in artificial intelligence, machine learning, neuroscience, medicine, cognitive science, psychology, linguistics, philosophy, education research and technology, and human-machine interaction. [1] Methods of inquiry in the brain and cognitive sciences are drawn from molecular, cellular, and systems neuroscience; cognitive and perceptual psychology; computer science and artificial intelligence; linguistics; philosophy of language and mind; and mathematics. [1] The undergraduate program is designed to provide instruction in the relevant aspects of these various disciplines. [1] Both brain science and cognitive science approaches examine perception, performance, and intervening processes in humans and animals. [1] Central issues in the discipline include the interpretation of sensory experience; the reception, manipulation, storage, and retrieval of information within the nervous system; and the planning and execution of motor activity. [1] Higher-level functions include the development of formal and informal reasoning skills; and the structure, acquisition, use, and internal representation of human language. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Analytics
Requirements: Application to MIT is centralized for all undergraduate programs. General requirements include the online application (which has its own biographical and essay sections), two letters of recommendation (one from a math/science teacher and one from a humanities, social science, or language teacher), and a secondary school report including an official high school transcript.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Business Analytics (BSBA) is for students with a strong interest and ability in math and computer science who want to apply these skills to challenging business problems and societal issues. Students learn techniques such as data modeling and analysis, optimization, and machine learning, so as to help businesses make improved decisions and design efficient processes. Electives provide the opportunity to learn additional methodologies, such as artificial intelligence, systems dynamics, and game theory; take advanced subjects in probability, statistics, and optimization; or study how analytics is applied in content areas such as operations, transportation, marketing, and finance.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: Application to MIT is done through their own application portal for all undergraduate programs. The general requirements include the online application form which has biographical information, five short-answer essays, and a list of activities. In addition, applicants must submit two letters of recommendation (one from a math or science teacher and another from a humanities, social science, or language teacher), a Secondary School Report (SSR) with an official high school transcript, and SAT or ACT scores. [8, 6]
Description: Overview.The bachelor of science (BS) in chemical engineering prepares students for an exciting field. Chemical engineers have traditionally been employed in chemical, petrochemical, agricultural chemical, pulp and paper, plastics, cosmetics, and textiles industries and in consulting and design firms. Today, chemical engineers also play an integral role in emerging biological and advanced materials fields, including nanotechnology. For example, chemical engineers are creating new materials needed for space exploration, alternative energy sources, and faster, self-powered computer chips. [7] Chemical engineers employ nanotechnology to revolutionize sensors, security systems, and medical diagnostics and treatments. [7] In addition to creating important products, chemical engineers are also involved in protecting our environment by exploring ways to reduce acid rain and smog; to recycle and reduce wastes; to develop new sources of environmentally clean energy; and to design inherently safe, efficient, and “green” processes. [7] The role of a chemical engineer is to develop new products and to design processes while reducing costs, increasing production, and improving the quality and safety of new products. [7] Upon completion, graduates with a BS in Chemical Engineering can move in several career directions. Traditionally, the degree prepares one for practice in the engineering and the control of processes involving chemicals, biotechnology feedstocks, and pharmaceuticals. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: When applying to MIT for a bachelor's degree, prospective students apply to the university as a whole, not to a specific major like Chemistry. [25] All first-year students begin as 'undeclared'. The general application requirements include completing the online MIT Application, which consists of biographical information, five short-answer essays, a section to list activities, and an academic section with a self-reported coursework form. [4] In addition to the application form, students must submit a Secondary School Report with their high school transcript and two letters of recommendation: one from a math or science teacher and one from a humanities, social science, or language teacher. [8] An interview with an MIT Educational Counselor is also a recommended part of the application process. [21]
ScholarshipAmount: The median MIT Scholarship was $69,777 for 2024–2025.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry and Biology
Requirements: MIT does not admit students to a specific major. Students are admitted to the institute as a whole and declare their major at the end of their first year. Application requirements for first-year admission include submitting an online application with five short-answer essays, two letters of recommendation (one from a math or science teacher and one from a humanities, social science, or language teacher), a Secondary School Report (SSR) with a high school transcript, and SAT or ACT scores. [6, 7, 8, 16]
Description: The Department of Biology and the Department of Chemistry offer a joint curriculum leading to a Bachelor of Science in Chemistry and Biology that focuses on the intersection of these two subject areas, encompassing biochemistry and chemical biology. The curriculum provides strong foundations in both biology and chemistry, with flexibility in elective subjects that enable students to tailor their major program to their specific interests within the broad interface of biology and chemistry. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Civil and Environmental Engineering
Requirements: MIT requires a single undergraduate application for all programs. The general requirements include: the application with essays and an activities list, two letters of recommendation (one from a math/science teacher and one from a humanities/language teacher), a school counselor recommendation, high school transcripts, and scores from either the SAT or ACT. [4, 7, 9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Climate System Science and Engineering
Requirements: At MIT, undergraduate students apply to the university as a whole, not to a specific program. They declare their major, such as the Bachelor of Science in Climate System Science and Engineering, after their first year. General application requirements include completing the online application, providing a high school transcript, and submitting two letters of recommendation: one from a math or science teacher and one from a humanities, social science, or language teacher. Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are also required.
Department: School of Engineering, School of Science
Concentration: ['climate mitigation and adaptation', 'computation and statistics', 'Earth systems', 'policy strategies and economics', 'AI and Data Science', 'Climate, Synthetic Biology and Food Security', 'Environmental Justice']
Description: Die Abteilung für Bau- und Umweltingenieurwesen und die Abteilung für Erd-, Atmosphären- und Planetenwissenschaften bieten einen gemeinsamen grundständigen Studiengang an, der zum Bachelor of Science in Climate System Science and Engineering führt. Der Lehrplan bereitet die Studierenden auf eine wachsende Zahl neuer Berufe in den Bereichen Klimawissenschaft und -technik, Klimarisikomodellierung sowie Klima- und Nachhaltigkeitspraktiken vor. Er vermittelt die notwendigen Werkzeuge, Methoden und wissenschaftlichen und technischen Prinzipien, um ein Verständnis für die Klimasysteme der Erde sowie für moderne Ansätze zur Abschwächung und Anpassung zu entwickeln. Der Bachelor of Science in Climate System Science and Engineering gewährleistet eine solide Grundlage in den notwendigen Grundlagenwissenschaften, Mathematik, Physik, Chemie und Biologie mit fortgeschrittenen Studien zur Erstellung quantitativer Modelle komplexer Erdsysteme, zur Analyse großer und vielfältiger klimabezogener Datensätze und zur Quantifizierung von Unsicherheiten in Klimamodellen, die bei politischen und Entscheidungsfindungen verwendet werden. Die Studierenden des Programms sind Vollmitglieder beider Abteilungen und der beiden Fakultäten für Ingenieurwissenschaften und Naturwissenschaften. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Comparative Media Studies
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: The program leading to the Bachelor of Science in Comparative Media Studies degree is designed to integrate the study of contemporary media (film, television, digital systems) with a broad historical understanding of older forms of human expression. [1, 8] The program embraces theoretical and interpretive principles drawn from the central humanistic disciplines of literary study, history, anthropology, art history, and film studies, but aims as well for a comparative synthesis that is responsive to the distinctive emerging media culture of the 21st century. [1, 8] Students explore the complexity of the media environment by learning to think across media, to see beyond the boundaries imposed by older medium-specific approaches to the study of audio-visual and literary forms. [1, 8] The undergraduate program serves as preparation for advanced study in a range of scholarly and professional disciplines and also for careers in media or industry. [1, 8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computation and Cognition
Department: Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) and Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences (BCS)
Description: The Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and the Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences offer a joint curriculum leading to a Bachelor of Science in Computation and Cognition that focuses on the emerging field of computational and engineering approaches to brain science, cognition, and machine intelligence. [2] The curriculum provides flexibility to accommodate students with a wide diversity of interests in this area—from biologically inspired approaches to artificial intelligence to reverse engineering circuits in the brain. [2, 6] This joint program prepares students for careers that include advanced applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning, as well as further graduate study in systems and cognitive neuroscience. [6, 9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Engineering
Concentration: ['Computer Science', 'Artificial Intelligence & Decision Making', 'Electrical Engineering']
Description: Course 6-3 centers on software engineering, computer systems, and theoretical computer science, and allows exploration into computer architecture, human-computer interaction and graphics, and artificial intelligence and machine learning. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Molecular Biology
Requirements: General application requirements for first-year admission to MIT apply to all undergraduate programs. MIT has its own application, which includes components for general information, essays, activities, and academics. [1, 3] Applicants are also required to submit transcripts and two letters of recommendation. [10]
Department: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Molecular Biology is a joint program offered by the Department of Biology and the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS), placing students in both the School of Science and the School of Engineering. [18]
Description: The Department of Biology and the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EEEC) offer a joint curriculum leading to a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Molecular Biology that focuses on the emerging field of computational and molecular biology. [1] The curriculum provides strong foundations in both biology and computer science and features innovative, integrative, capstone, and elective subjects. The goal is to produce an entirely new cadre of graduates who are uniquely qualified to address the challenges and opportunities at the interface of computational and molecular biology. [1] The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Molecular Biology prepares students for careers that leverage computational biology (e.g., pharmaceuticals, bioinformatics, medicine, etc.) as well as further graduate study in biology, in computer science, and in emerging programs at the interface. [1] Students in the program are full members of both departments and of two schools, Science and Engineering, with one academic advisor from each department. [1]
ScholarshipType: MIT offers need-based financial aid, and scholarships are a component of the aid package. The university also lists various other scholarship opportunities. [38]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Economics, and Data Science
Requirements: MIT has its own application, available online from mid-August through January 1. [2] The application includes general information, five short answer essays (about 200 words each), and a list of four activities. [4] Applicants must also submit a Secondary School Report (SSR) with a high school transcript, and two letters of recommendation: one from a math or science teacher and another from a humanities, social science, or language teacher. [4] Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are also required. [6]
Department: The Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and the Department of Economics offer a joint curriculum leading to a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Economics and Data Science (Course 6-14). [7]
Description: The Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and the Department of Economics offer a joint curriculum leading to a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Economics, and Data Science (Course 6-14). [6] The interdisciplinary major provides students a portfolio of skills in economics, computing, and data science that are increasingly valued in both the business world and academia. [6] The economics and computer science disciplines have a substantial overlap both in their reliance on game theory and mathematical modeling techniques and their use of data analytics. [6] The economics side of the program includes subjects in microeconomic theory and econometrics and electives that expose students to how economists in various fields use mathematical models and statistical evidence to think about problems. [6] The computer science side includes a number of subjects that develop complementary knowledge, including the study of algorithms, optimization, and machine learning (which is increasingly integrated with econometrics). [6] The program also includes coursework in several mathematical subjects, including linear algebra, probability, discrete mathematics, and statistics, which can be taken in various departments. [6] The Course 6-14 major is also well suited to students whose primary interest is in game theory and mathematical modeling. [6] It can prepare students for graduate study in either discipline. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences
Concentration: ['Earth Science', 'Climate, Atmospheres + Oceans', 'Planetary Science + Astronomy', 'Environmental Science']
Description: Departmental programs apply physics, chemistry, and mathematics to the study of the Earth and planets in order to understand the processes that are active in the Earth's interior, oceans, and atmosphere, as well as the interiors and atmospheres of other planets. [1] The department also uses the basic sciences to understand the past history of the Earth and planets. By combining the past history with models of present physical, biological, and chemical processes, faculty and students work to develop an understanding of the dynamics of systems as diverse as the global climate system, regional tectonics and deformation, petroleum and geothermal reservoirs, and the solar system. [1] Research in the department is fundamental in nature, but underpins many of the most pressing societal questions of our time: climate and environmental change; natural hazards; natural resources; the origins of life both on Earth and elsewhere. [1] The curriculum for the Bachelor of Science in Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences ensures a fundamental background through general departmental subjects and advanced study in a concentration area chosen by the student. [1, 2] The student and advisor plan an appropriate and relevant selection of electives. [1, 2] Students are also required to take field and/or laboratory subjects, and to complete an independent research project as part of the degree requirements. [1, 2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Economics
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: Course 14-1, leading to the Bachelor of Science in Economics, provides students with a breadth and depth of training in economics that is unusual at the undergraduate level. It combines training in technical economics with in-depth exploration of students areas of interest. Students choose from a diverse set of upper-level undergraduate subjects and are encouraged to engage in independent research. [36] The aims of the SB in Economics degree program are threefold: to give students a firm grounding in economic theory and data analysis, to develop in-depth knowledge of particular economic issues, and to develop students capabilities for independent research. [36] These aims correspond roughly to the requirements in the Course 14-1 program of theory, statistics and econometrics, electives, and research. [36] The requirements allow substantial freedom for students in designing individual programs within economics and in balancing the program with subjects in other disciplines. [36]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Requirements: For undergraduate applicants, the general application requirements include a biographical information section, essays, an activities list, and academic transcripts. Applicants are also required to have two letters of recommendation: one from a math or science teacher and one from a humanities, social science, or language teacher. For graduate applicants, general requirements are not listed at an institute-level; applicants are directed to the individual department or program for specific requirements.
Description: A flexible combination of subjects, this major includes a focus on the areas in which both EE and CS overlap. [2] Students who entered MIT in Fall 2021 or later will complete the updated 6-2 degree program. [2] The program requires a foundation of fundamental subjects in programming, algorithms, and math, built upon with system design subjects, an integrative system design laboratory class, and elective subjects from various tracks. [2, 4] Starting in Fall 2024, the 6-2 Electrical Engineering and Computer Science degree program will be renamed and renumbered as 6-5 Electrical Engineering with Computing. [2]
Accredidation: The Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (Course 6-2) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Electrical Engineering, and by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Computer Science. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Science and Engineering
Description: The 6-1 program leads to the Bachelor of Science in Electrical Science and Engineering. The program starts with three foundation courses in circuits, signal processing, and computer architecture. Those are followed by specialization in three header subjects chosen from signals, nanoelectronics, electromagnetics, neurophysiology, or machine learning; two advanced undergraduate subjects; and two elective subjects from an extensive set of possibilities. [7]
Accredidation: The 6-1 program leads to the Bachelor of Science in Electrical Science and Engineering. It is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET. [2, 3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering (2-ENG) is a flexible engineering degree for students who wish to pursue a course of study that is not accommodated by one of the other undergraduate degrees in the School of Engineering. The program is designed by the student in consultation with a faculty advisor. The 2-ENG program allows students to combine the deep fundamentals of mechanical engineering with another area of interest. This program must contain a coherent set of subjects that meets an educational goal and that has a strong engineering component. The 2-ENG program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering (Course 2-ENG) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in History
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences (SHASS)
Description: The program leading to the degree of Bachelor of Science in History is designed to encourage students to discover and reconstruct the past, to confront and understand the complexity of past human behavior for itself, and to inform their sense of the historical present. [2, 6, 8] The curriculum includes the selection of at least one subject taken from the curriculum's 21H undergraduate seminars. [2, 6, 8] Students are expected to take seven additional subjects of their own choice, selected in consultation with a major advisor. [2, 6, 8] These must include subjects drawn from at least two geographical areas, as well as one pre-modern (before 1700) and one modern subject. [2, 8] During the junior year, the history major is required to take subject 21H.390 Theories and Methods in the Study of History, which is intended to develop skills for independent research and writing, followed in the senior year by 21H.THT History Pre-Thesis Tutorial and 21H.THU History Thesis. [2, 6]

[5, 8] An interview with a member of the MIT Educational Council is also highly recommended. [7, 13]

[1] One component is selected from the undergraduate degree curriculum of an engineering department, which is approved by a faculty member in the field. [1] The other component consists of subjects in a humanities field, chosen by the student in consultation with an advisor from the appropriate humanities faculty. [1] This unique arrangement yields a humanities program of considerable depth while allowing for continued serious commitment to an engineering interest. [1, 3] In most cases, a senior thesis or sequence of advanced seminars is also required. [3]
