ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Linguistics
Requirements: Application requirements for undergraduate programs at MIT are not specific to the Bachelor of Science in Linguistics and are the same for all prospective first-year students. Applicants must submit their application through MIT's own application portal. [4] The application includes biographical information, essays, a list of activities, academic transcripts, and two letters of recommendation. [7] An interview is also part of the process. [2] There is no mention of a required resume, formal statement of purpose, or writing sample for general undergraduate admission.
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description:
The Department of Linguistics and Philosophy currently offers two undergraduate programs leading to the degree of Bachelor of Science. Program 1 is offered by the Philosophy section of the department. The Linguistics Track of Program 2 is offered by the Linguistics section.  

Program _in Language and Mind_  
Program 2, also known as the Program in Language and Mind, aims to provide students with a working knowledge of a variety of issues that currently occupy the intersection of philosophy, linguistics, and cognitive science. Central among these topics are the nature of language, of those mental representations that we call “knowledge” and “belief,” and of the innate basis for the acquisition of certain types of knowledge (especially linguistic knowledge). Students have the option of pursuing either a philosophy track or a linguistics track. Both require a core set of subjects drawn from both fields and are designed to teach students the central facts and issues in the study of language and the representation of knowledge. Each track requires, in addition, a set of subjects drawn primarily from its discipline and is designed to prepare students for graduate study either in philosophy/cognitive science or in linguistics. A coherent program of three restricted electives (drawn from one or two of the following three areas: linguistics, philosophy, or a related area) rounds out the major.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Literature
Requirements: General application requirements for MIT vary significantly between undergraduate and graduate programs. For undergraduate applicants, the required materials include a biographical form, essays, a list of activities, and academic transcripts. For graduate applicants, general requirements are not specified at the institute level; instead, applicants must consult the individual department for its specific requirements, which may include a statement of purpose, letters of recommendation, and a resume/CV.

Description: The program in Literature leading to the Bachelor of Science in Literature is equivalent to the curricula in English (or literary studies) at major liberal arts institutions. [2, 5] The Literature curriculum is notable also for its integration of materials drawn from film and media, popular culture, and minority and ethnic cultures. [2, 5, 7] The major consists of at least 10 subjects, including no more than three introductory subjects, at least three intermediate subjects, and at least three seminars. [2, 5, 7] A minimum of three subjects in the overall degree program must focus primarily on material prior to 1900. [2, 7] The curriculum emphasizes interdisciplinary approaches to literary texts as well as theoretical, generic, and thematic subjects that range across geographical and historical boundaries. [5, 6] The Literature Section accommodates students with a wide variety of interests and diverse career choices. [5, 6] The major provides a solid grounding in the discipline but remains flexible enough to allow students to explore the particular domains that most interest them. [5, 6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Management
Requirements: MIT does not have a general, institute-level list of required application documents such as a resume or statement of purpose for all graduate programs; these requirements are set at the departmental or program level. For first-year (undergraduate) applications, the general requirements include essays, a description of activities, academic transcripts, and letters of recommendation.
Concentration: Students can select from a defined concentration or create their own tailored concentration with the approval of their faculty advisor and the MIT Sloan Undergraduate Office. At least three of the concentration electives must be Course 15 subjects. [7]
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Management (Course 15-1) provides students with an innovative business education that is comprehensive and flexible. [8] Students begin with coursework that builds a strong foundation in probability and statistics, managerial communication, managerial psychology, microeconomics, and accounting. [8] They augment this foundation by selecting two restricted electives in core business functions: finance, operations management, marketing, and strategy. [6] Students then tailor the remainder of their program by selecting five electives that go into depth in an individualized concentration area. [8]
Accredidation: The MIT Sloan School of Management is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). [2, 13, 16]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
Description: The Course 3 curriculum leading to a Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering includes the General Institute Requirements as well as Course 3 required core subjects and a capstone project. The Course 3 core subjects address the fundamental relationships between processing, microstructure, properties, and performance of modern materials and their applications. Students choose from a sequence of restricted electives that provide more specialized coverage of the major classes of modern materials: biomaterials, ceramics, electronic materials, metals, and polymers, as well as cross-cutting topics relevant to all types of materials. Participation in laboratory work by undergraduates is an integral part of the curriculum.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering (Course 3) is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Materials Engineering. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Economics
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Economics (Course 14-2) is designed for students who desire a deeper mathematical foundation. [6, 18] It allows them to concentrate in a subset of economics topics. [18] The program provides the strong mathematical and theoretical preparation needed for subsequent graduate study in economics. [6] Students majoring in Mathematical Economics begin with the same introductory micro and macro courses as other economics majors but then undertake a program with rigorous mathematical training in microeconomic theory and econometrics, along with substantial coursework in mathematics, including real analysis, linear algebra or differential equations, and a mathematics seminar. [6] This program is particularly well-suited for students with an interest in mathematical microeconomic theory or econometrics. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
Concentration: ['General Mathematics', 'Applied Mathematics', 'Pure Mathematics']
Description: There are three undergraduate programs that lead to the degree Bachelor of Science in Mathematics (Course 18): General Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, and Pure Mathematics. The General Mathematics option is the most flexible and offers a broad education with a theoretical emphasis. The Applied Mathematics track adds an interdisciplinary concentration in a related field. The Pure Mathematics track is intended for students seeking a strong foundation in the theory of modern mathematics. There is also a separate degree for a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics with Computer Science (Course 18C). [18]

Description: The undergraduate program leading to the degree of Bachelor of Science in Music comprises a grounding in foundational skills in music history and culture, performance, and music theory and a capstone Advanced Seminar. [6] The Music Program offers a broad range of opportunities to experience and engage critically with all areas of music. Introductory classes (21M.0XX) assume no previous knowledge of reading or performing music, but all with the exception of Fundamentals of Music (21M.051) are appropriate for advanced musicians as well. Most non-introductory subjects are arranged into one of three categories: history/culture (21M.2XX), composition/theory (21M.3XX), and performance (21M.4XX). Subjects in music and technology are distributed throughout the curriculum. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Theater Arts
Description: An undergraduate program leading to the Bachelor of Science in Theater Arts degree is also offered. It comprises a broad foundation in theoretical and practical studies, and intensive performance and design practica. To satisfy the requirements of the major, students complete a coherent set of restricted elective subjects (two of which satisfy the CI-M requirement). A capstone thesis (including a pre-thesis tutorial) is an optional component of the major. With an emphasis on artistic practice, this course of study prepares students who plan either to enter the field or to pursue graduate studies in theater arts. Students should demonstrate proficiency in theater arts fundamentals, and should have some performance experience before declaring the major. Consultation with the major advisor in Theater Arts is required no later than the first term of the junior year.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Urban Science and Planning with Computer Science

The general application includes a biographical form, essays, a list of activities, and academic transcripts. Applicants also need to submit two letters of recommendation: one from a math or science teacher and one from a humanities, social science, or language teacher.

[2] For non-native English speakers applying as undergraduates who have used English for less than 5 years or do not speak it at home or in school, submitting English proficiency exam results is strongly recommended. [6] Required subjects include 21W.THT Writing Pre-Thesis Tutorial and 21W.THU Writing Program Thesis (CI-M). [6] Joint degree programs in Writing are also offered in combination with a field in engineering (21E) or science (21S). [7]

ProgramName: Minor in African and African Diaspora Studies
Requirements: To be admitted as a regular graduate student at MIT, an applicant must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited college, university, or technical school of acceptable standing. [6] For undergraduate admissions, while there are no specific required high school classes, applicants are expected to have undertaken a rigorous program. [13]
Concentration: While the program does not list formally named concentrations, students may concentrate on a particular region or on any of the broad groupings of African cultures, regions or language groups. [3, 5] Students choosing to focus on the African diaspora may concentrate on African American studies or on any group of African-descended populations in the Americas or elsewhere—be it in the US, in the Caribbean, or anywhere else in the Americas and beyond. [3, 5]
Description: The Minor in African and African Diaspora Studies is designed for students interested in the contributions, cultures, and experiences of the peoples of African descent on the African continent and across the Diaspora. [3, 5] The goal of the minor program is to emphasize the importance of Africa and people of African descent in world's cultural, economic, and social developments, and to provide a balance between language, humanistic, historical, and contemporary study. [3, 5] Building on MIT's strengths in understanding science and technology, the minor provides students the opportunity to study interactions of people of African descent with contemporary technology sectors such as digital media, artificial intelligence, aerospace, genetics, and climate mitigation efforts. [3, 5] The minor includes study of economic and political systems as they reflect the African continent and areas of the African diaspora, and the histories, languages, and literatures of Africans and peoples of African descent elsewhere. [3, 5] All of Africa falls within the geographical scope of the minor. [3, 5] Students focusing on either principal area (Africa or the African diaspora) must also take at least one subject which deals with the other area or with interactions between them. [3, 5] The minor consists of six subjects (at least three of which must be MIT subjects), arranged in four areas of study: Area I: Language; Area II: Humanities and the Arts; Area III: Social Sciences; Area IV: Historical Studies. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in American Studies
Requirements: The minor consists of six subjects (at least three of which must be MIT subjects), from at least two of the following three disciplinary areas: Area I: Humanities and the Arts; Area II: Social Sciences; Science, Technology, and Society; Area III: Historical Studies. [9] Five of the six minor subjects may be counted toward the eight-subject Institute HASS Requirement. [9] Of the six subjects required for the minor, at least four cannot be counted toward a major or another minor. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Ancient and Medieval Studies
Requirements: The minor in Ancient and Medieval Studies consists of six subjects, with at least three being MIT subjects. These subjects are arranged in four primary areas of study: Area I: Languages, Area II: Arts and Architecture, Area III: Literary Studies, and Area IV: Historical, Social, and Philosophical Studies. Students are required to demonstrate intermediate level language proficiency in Greek, Latin, or a medieval vernacular. At least four of the six subjects for the minor cannot be counted toward a major or another minor. [4, 9]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: The Minor in Ancient and Medieval Studies provides a curricular framework for exploring a wide variety of topics related to ancient and medieval studies, drawing from multiple disciplines. [3] The program covers a chronological span of approximately 6,500 years, from 5000 BC to 1500 AD. [3] Its goal is to foster an understanding of the distant past, both for its intrinsic value and as a subject for modern inquiry. [3] The curriculum delves into the history of ideas, institutions, material artifacts, literature, and original languages. [3] It examines the structure of institutions and social systems, as well as the interplay between social order and learned traditions, values, and ideologies. [3] The program is designed for students who wish to gain a deeper understanding of the forces that shaped the ancient and medieval worlds, with a broad geographical and chronological scope that encourages comparative study. [3] Subject matter ranges from Classical Greece and Rome and ancient societies in Asia and South America to medieval Europe and Japan. [3] Students are required to demonstrate intermediate proficiency in Greek, Latin, or a medieval vernacular language and are encouraged to create a coherent program of study in consultation with a minor advisor. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Anthropology
Description: MIT Anthropology offers undergraduate students exposure to diverse human cultures, providing perspectives relevant to other fields in the humanities, social sciences, sciences, and engineering. Our courses offer conceptual tools for cross-cultural understanding and train students to think critically about the dynamism of specific cultural forms. Subjects also provide an intensive introduction to areas of faculty specializations, including medical anthropology, the social dimensions of science, technology and computing, material culture studies, environmental movements, food cultures and politics, magic and religion, ethnographic film production, gender and family studies, migration and ethnic identity, and urban studies. The Minor in Anthropology consists of six subjects. Students create individual programs with the help of the minor advisor to ensure that they gain a coherent understanding of the methods, approaches, and some of the results of the discipline. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Applied International Studies
Requirements: General application requirements for graduate admissions at MIT are not centralized and vary significantly by department and program. Most applications require letters of recommendation and a personal statement or essay. [6] For undergraduate admissions, applicants must submit their high school transcript and letters of recommendation. While not explicitly a 'resume', applicants are encouraged to list their extracurricular activities. Many graduate programs may also require a resume or curriculum vitae, but this is not an institute-level requirement.
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences (SHASS). [4, 7]
Fees: There is no separate tuition fee for a minor program. The full cost of attendance for an undergraduate student for the 2025–2026 academic year is $89,340. [2]
Description: The Minor in Applied International Studies is designed to help students integrate a practical, applied international experience into a coherent course of study. The minor is built around four key components: Local understanding with a global perspective. Theory combined with in-the-field experience. Cross-cultural communication skills. Independent research. The result is a comprehensive plan of study that allows students to combine academic work with foreign experience to gain the skills and perspective necessary for a productive, sustainable career in the global economy. The Minor in Applied International Studies consists of six internationally-oriented subjects from any program in the School of Humanities, Art, and Social Sciences, including: At least two subjects focused on one area of the world, including at least one in the social sciences. Qualifying subjects will be determined with the help of the minor advisor. The equivalent of four semesters of college language training related to the student's geographical specialization. Upper-level language subjects (beyond first-year subjects) may count toward the six-subject total. An intensive international experience (MISTI, D-Lab, or other experience for at least two months). A research seminar in international studies and social science, 17.591 Research Seminar in Applied International Studies.
AverageScholarshipAmount: The median MIT Scholarship was $69,777 for the 2024–2025 academic year. [18]
ScholarshipAmount: For the 2025–2026 academic year, students from families with an income under $200,000 a year (with typical assets) will receive an MIT Scholarship that covers at least the cost of tuition. [2, 26]

ProgramName: Minor in Archaeology and Materials
Requirements: The Minor in Archaeology and Materials consists of six undergraduate subjects: 3.010 Structure of Materials, 3.020 Thermodynamics of Materials, 3.030 Microstructural Evolution in Materials, 3.985[J] Archaeological Science, and 3.986[J] The Human Past: Introduction to Archaeology, plus one elective subject. [10] To declare the minor, a student must complete an application form in consultation with the minor advisor. [5]
Department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
Description: The Minor in Archaeology and Materials (3-C) is designed to afford students broad exposure to fields that contribute fundamental theoretical and methodological approaches to the study of ancient and historic societies. The primary fields include anthropological archaeology, geology, and materials science and engineering. The program enriches knowledge of past and present-day nonindustrial societies by making the natural and engineering sciences part of the archaeological tool kit. [4] The program's special focus is on understanding prehistoric culture through study of the structure and properties of materials associated with human activities. Investigating peoples' interactions with materials, the objects that such interactions produced, and the related environmental settings leads to a fuller analysis of the physical, social, cultural, and ideological world in which people function. [4]
Accredidation: The department does not seek ABET accreditation for the 3-C program. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Art, Culture, and Technology
Requirements: The HASS Minor in Art, Culture and Technology consists of six subjects arranged into three levels of study. Students must take two subjects from Tier I, three from Tier II, and one from Tier III. [2, 5]
Description: The HASS Minor in Art, Culture, and Technology is designed to explore the conjunction of art with culture, science, technology, and design, and to develop critical and production practices. [1] The minor consists of six subjects arranged into three levels of study. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Asian and Asian Diaspora Studies
Requirements: To declare a Minor in Asian and Asian Diaspora Studies, a student must meet with the minor advisor to plan their program of study and complete a HASS Minor Application Form. [9, 10] The minor consists of six subjects. [1] Students must designate their minor between the end of their sophomore year and Add Date one full term prior to receiving their degree. [9]
Description: The Minor in Asian and Asian Diaspora Studies is designed for students interested in the language, history, politics, and culture of Asia and/or the Asian diasporas. [1, 2] In consultation with the minor advisor, students may focus their coursework on a subregion of Asia, on one of the Asian diasporas, or design their program to offer a comparative study across different regions and/or cultural groups. [1, 2] The goal of the minor program is to provide balanced coverage of language, humanistic and social science offerings on the region, and to expose students to comparative perspectives. [1, 2] The minor consists of six subjects (at least three of which must be MIT subjects), arranged in four areas of study: Area I: Language; Area II: Humanities and the Arts; Area III: Social Sciences; Area IV: Historical Studies. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Astronomy
Requirements: Information about the application process for a minor in Astronomy is not available on the MIT website. The website lists the subject requirements to complete the minor, which total 72 units. These requirements include introductory physics and mathematics subjects, as well as core and elective subjects in astronomy and astrophysics. The process for declaring a minor is an internal process for enrolled MIT students and does not require a separate application in the way that admission to the university does.
Description: The Minor in Astronomy, offered jointly by the Department of Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences and the Department of Physics, covers the observational and theoretical foundations. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Bible Studies
Requirements: To fulfill the requirements for the Religious Studies Concentration, students must take three subjects that form a coherent course of study, selected in consultation with the concentration advisor. [2] Students must submit a HASS Concentration Form on WebSIS to declare their field of study and the subjects they plan to take. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Biological Engineering
Requirements: To declare a minor at MIT, a student must complete an application form in consultation with the appropriate minor advisor. [5] For the Biomedical Engineering minor, application forms are available in the BE Academic Office (Room 16-267). [2] Students should meet with their department's BME advisor to plan their program of study and then submit the completed, signed application form for final approval. [2] Students should apply by the end of their sophomore year and no later than "Add Date" of the spring term of their junior year. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Biology
Requirements: To complete the minor, a student must have credit for five subjects, including 7.012 Introductory Biology, 7.013 Introductory Biology, 7.014 Introductory Biology, 7.015 Introductory Biology, or 7.016 Introductory Biology; 7.03 Genetics; 7.05 General Biochemistry; one of the following labs: 7.102[J] Introduction to Experimental Biology & Communication, 7.103[J] Applied Molecular Biology Laboratory, 7.340[J] Advanced Undergraduate Seminar in Biological Chemistry, or 7.341[J] Advanced Undergraduate Seminar in Biological Chemistry; and one additional subject in biology.

ProgramName: Minor in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: To declare the Minor in Biomedical Engineering, an enrolled MIT undergraduate student must meet with their department's BME advisor to plan their program of study. The student must then submit the completed and signed application form. [2] The program requires a total of seven subjects selected from categories including Mathematics, Human Physiology, and Biomedical Engineering and Applications. [8] A maximum of four subjects taken for the minor can also count toward a major or another minor. [8]
Description: The goal of the BME Minor program is to educate students in how to apply fundamental engineering principles to solve challenging problems in biology and medicine. [3] The BME Minor program aims to guide students to gain an appreciation of diverse biomedical engineering sub-disciplines via coursework, which relates math, physiology, and engineering electives drawn from many different disciplines, reflecting interdepartmental nature of modern biomedical engineering. [3] The Biomedical Engineering Minor (BME) program requires a total of seven subjects selected from a series of categories as outlined below. [8]

ProgramName: Minor in Brain and Cognitive Sciences
Requirements: To declare the Minor in Brain and Cognitive Sciences, the Minor Application should be filled out by the end of the student's sophomore year, but no later than Add Date one full term before the term in which the student expects to receive the S.B. degree. Students should visit the Registrar's website to print the Minor Application form and email bcs-undergrad-admin@mit.edu to arrange a meeting to discuss the application and minor completion. An unofficial transcript is required for this meeting. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Business Analytics
Minor in Chemistry
Requirements: A minor in chemistry can be earned by completing 72 units in Chemistry. For a general description of the Minor Program, refer to the MIT Course Bulletin's information on Minors and for general guidelines refer to the information on Declaring a Minor from the Registrar's Office. [10]
Description: A minor in chemistry can be earned by completing 72 units in Chemistry. [2] For a general description of the Minor Program, refer to the MIT Course Bulletin's information on Minors and for general guidelines refer to the information on Declaring a Minor from the Registrar's Office. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Chinese
Requirements: The Minor Program in Chinese consists of six subjects. Students must consult with the appropriate minor advisor to develop a course plan and submit a completed HASS Minor Application Form. [6] The program is for students who have already reached an intermediate level of proficiency (third semester or above), and beginner courses such as Chinese I and II do not count toward the minor. [3] The six subjects are typically distributed among three tiers: Tier I (intermediate language), Tier II (advanced language), and Tier III (subjects in Chinese literature, history, or culture). [3] Of the six subjects required, a maximum of five may also be counted toward the eight-subject HASS Requirement. [9]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: As MIT students pursue an expanding spectrum of international engagements, Global Languages classes and immersive international experiences help prepare them to live and work in the diverse and multilingual context of a globalizing world. [2, 7] Through our curriculum, students develop communicative and intercultural competencies, critical thinking skills, intellectual curiosity, diversity awareness, and cross-cultural understanding. [2, 7]

ProgramName: Minor in Civil and Environmental Engineering
Requirements:
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) offers three distinct minors. A minor generally consists of five to seven subjects. [18, 21] According to the official MIT website, students wishing to declare a minor must complete an application form in consultation with the appropriate minor advisor. [18, 21] There are no additional admission procedures to declare a minor for enrolled students. [23]

The specific minors and their required subjects are as follows:

1.  Minor in Civil Engineering: This minor focuses on subjects including solid and fluid mechanics, materials, and new labs. The required subjects are: 1.035 Multiscale Characterization of Materials, 1.036 Structural Mechanics and Design, 1.050 Solid Mechanics, 1.060A Fluid Mechanics I, 1.060B Fluid Mechanics II, 1.101 Introduction to Civil and Environmental Engineering Design I, and 1.102 Introduction to Civil and Environmental Engineering Design II. [17]
2.  Minor in Civil and Environmental Systems: This minor combines principles from civil, environmental, and systems engineering. The required subjects are: 1.011 Project Evaluation and Management, 1.020 Engineering Sustainability: Analysis and Design, 1.022 Introduction to Network Models, 1.041 Transportation Systems Modeling, 1.075 Water Resource Systems, 1.101 Introduction to Civil and Environmental Engineering Design I, and 1.102 Introduction to Civil and Environmental Engineering Design II. [16, 17]
3.  Minor in Environmental Engineering Science: This minor requires fieldwork as part of the Traveling Research Environmental Experiences (TREX) program. The required subjects include: 1.018AJ Fundamentals of Ecology I, 1.060A Fluid Mechanics I, 1.061A Transport Processes in the Environment I, 1.070AJ Introduction to Hydrology and Water Resources, 1.089A Environmental Microbiology, 1.091 and 1.092 Traveling Research Environmental eXperience (TREX), 1.106 Environmental Fluid Transport Processes and Hydrology Laboratory, and 1.107 Environmental Chemistry and Biology Laboratory. [17]

ProgramName: Minor in Civil Engineering
Description: The Civil Engineering Minor offers subjects that reflect the wide extent of education that now encompasses the field, including solid and fluid mechanics, materials, and new labs. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Climate System Science and Engineering
Minor in Comparative Media Studies
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: The Comparative Media Studies minor requires six subjects: one introductory, one intermediate, one capstone, and three electives. [2] The undergraduate program in Comparative Media Studies offers students an opportunity for interdisciplinary study of film, television, game design, virtual worlds, digital artworks, civic media, interactive writing, and other communications media. [3] The program is designed to integrate the study of contemporary media (film, television, digital systems) with a broad historical understanding of older forms of human expression. It embraces theoretical and interpretive principles from humanistic disciplines like literary study, history, anthropology, art history, and film studies, aiming for a comparative synthesis that responds to the emerging media culture of the 21st century. [4] Students learn to think across media and see beyond boundaries imposed by older, medium-specific approaches. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Computer Science and Engineering
Requirements: MIT's graduate admissions are decentralized, with each department setting its own specific application requirements and deadlines. [2] To apply, prospective students can create an account on the application website and choose their desired department and degree program. [2] Most graduate departments utilize a unified application portal, while the Sloan School of Management has a separate one. [2] Generally, applicants will need to provide transcripts, letters of recommendation, standardized test scores, and a statement of purpose or admissions essay. [1] However, it is essential to review the specific requirements for each program as they can differ even within the university. [1]
Description: Computational thinking is an essential skill in all engineering and scientific disciplines. The Minor in Computer Science willlipidemia you with both depth and breadth in the field, as well as the opportunity to explore areas of their own interest. You'll complete six subjects (totaling at least 72 units) including at least one software-intensive subject, at least one algorithms-intensive subject, and at least one advanced subject. Upon completion of the minor you'll have the knowledge and skills needed to make effective use of computer science concepts and computing technology in your future career. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Computer Science, Economics, and Data Science
Requirements: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) does not offer a specific 'Minor in Computer Science, Economics, and Data Science'. It offers a Bachelor of Science (S.B.) major in this field, known as Course 6-14. [4] The general process for declaring any minor at MIT, for enrolled students, involves meeting with the minor advisor for the chosen field to plan the program and completing an application form. [2] There are no application requirements such as a resume, statement of purpose, or test scores for declaring a minor.

ProgramName: Minor in Control, Instrumentation, and Robotics
Requirements: For first-year and transfer applicants, the application requirements include a biographical information section and sections for essays, activities, and academics. There are two short essays, each with a word count of 200–250 words. Applicants are also asked to list up to four activities. For academics, applicants should list the subjects they have taken in high school and any scores from standardized tests like the SAT or ACT. Additionally, two letters of recommendation are required: one from a math or science teacher and one from a humanities, social science, or language teacher.

ProgramName: Minor in Design
Requirements: The general guidelines for a minor program at MIT state that it consists of five to seven subjects. A student should apply for a minor by the end of their sophomore year, but no later than Add Date one full term before graduation, by completing an application form in consultation with the appropriate minor advisor. The Minor in Design (also known as D-Minor) was established by the Department of Architecture. After taking three foundational design courses, students choose three electives from categories like Design Technology and Computation or Arts and Culture.
ScholarshipType: Need-based grants, scholarships, and student loans are available to MIT undergraduates.

ProgramName: Minor in Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences
Requirements: The EAPS Minor requires a solid foundation in two core subjects plus electives that create expertise in a particular area. Opportunities for field work, laboratory work, and independent study are an essential component of the minor. [5, 7] Students must complete an application form for the minor in consultation with the minor advisor. [6, 9] The minor program consists of five to seven subjects. [2, 6] To declare, students must meet with the minor advisor to plan their program and complete an application, bringing an unofficial transcript to the meeting. [2]
Department: Department of Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences

ProgramName: Minor in Economics
Requirements: To earn a minor in Economics, a student must complete six subjects: 14.01 Principles of Microeconomics, 14.02 Principles of Macroeconomics, one statistics subject (from a list including 14.30, 18.05, 1.010), one Tier 2 intermediate subject (from a list including 14.03, 14.04, 14.05), and two Tier 3 advanced elective subjects. [3]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Minor in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Department: The Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) is jointly operated by the School of Engineering and the Schwarzman College of Computing.
Fees: A specific tuition fee for the minor program is not mentioned. The program is taken by students enrolled in a bachelor's degree program, and the general undergraduate tuition would apply.

ProgramName: Minor in Energy Studies
Requirements: To declare a Minor in Energy Studies, the student must meet with the minor advisor to plan a program of study and complete an application form. [6] A copy of the student's unofficial transcript should be brought to the meeting. [6] Minor programs generally consist of five to seven subjects. [6] A minimum of three subjects (or 36 units) taken for the Energy Studies Minor cannot also count toward a student's major or other minor. [1]
Description: Developed and administered by the MIT Energy Initiative, the Energy Studies Minor sets students on the path to tackle the world's complex climate and energy challenges. [4] Through the minor, students build strong foundational knowledge of diverse energy topics while benefiting from hands-on learning opportunities to work with world-renowned researchers, policy analysts, and thought leaders. [4] Students also make groundbreaking discoveries and prepare for exciting careers in industry, government, and academia. [4] The Energy Studies Minor complements the deep expertise obtained in any MIT major with broad, interdisciplinary training in science, technology, and the social sciences, including policy issues surrounding energy and climate change. [1] Students take classes in four core areas, plus 24 units of electives. [1] The core consists of: Science Foundations: fundamental laws and principles that govern energy sources, conversion, and uses; Economics Foundations: how economic principles underlie every aspect of energy; Social Science Foundations: social scientific perspectives that help explain human behavior in an energy context, and; Energy Technology/Engineering in Context: the application of laws and principles to a specific energy context. [1] The elective component (generally two classes) allows students to focus on their individual areas of interest. [1]

ProgramName: Minor in Entrepreneurship and Innovation
Requirements: To declare a minor at MIT, you must meet with the minor advisor in your chosen field to plan your program of study and complete an application form; you should bring a copy of your unofficial transcript to this meeting. [3, 10] The Minor in Entrepreneurship and Innovation requires the completion of five courses: a core curriculum of two E&I Foundations subjects and an elective in each of the three following domains: E&I in Context, Leadership of Teams and Organizations, and E&I Experiential. [5, 12] A minimum of three subjects (or 36 units) taken for the minor cannot also be counted toward a student's major or another minor. [12]
Description: The Minor in Entrepreneurship and Innovation (E&I Minor) educates students to serve as leaders in the innovation economy with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to develop, scale, and deliver breakthrough solutions to real-world problems. They will be prepared to do so within a range of organizational contexts: an entrepreneurial start-up of their own, as key members of a founding team, or as an entrepreneurial member of a large organization. [1] Jointly offered by the Schools of Engineering and Management, the minor is designed as an interdisciplinary program with a coherent combination of conceptual and practical elements that draws on a wealth of prior educational activities in this domain. [1] Students who complete the E&I Minor will have developed knowledge and skills in: The innovation process from the conception of an initial invention and the problem it may solve to the refinement of the solution, to the considerations needed in the scale-up and delivery of the solution, to the launch of an appropriately funded entity. [1] Strategies and methods to engage in rigorous iterations to identify and deeply understand societal needs/problems and develop robust, scalable solutions. Types of organizational models and designs for the delivery of innovations to the world. A range of global contexts for entrepreneurship and innovation, including variations in the interface with key stakeholders whose interests may enable or limit the potential effectiveness of innovation and entrepreneurship. [1]

ProgramName: Minor in Environment and Sustainability
Requirements: The program is a minor, which is declared by current students rather than applied to. It is open to all MIT undergraduates in any major. The requirements to obtain the minor involve completing five to six subjects for a minimum of 57 units, including a foundational subject, subjects in two core areas (Context and Perspective, and Sustainable Solutions), and 24 units of elective subjects. [1, 6]
Description: Open to all MIT undergraduates in any major, the Environment and Sustainability Minor (E&S Minor) offers students the opportunity to apply their STEM and major-course knowledge to some of the most critical and challenging problems facing humanity. [2] The minor equips students with interdisciplinary knowledge and real-world experience needed to understand, diagnose, and develop solutions to complex problems faced by society as it strives for social and environmental sustainability. [2] Students tailor their MIT education to their professional goals, preparing to apply the principles of sustainability in diverse workplace contexts, including business/industry, government, civil society, and academia. [2] The E&S Minor combines a wide range of fields of inquiry to directly engage environmental and climate challenges facing ecosystems and populations around the globe. [2] Fundamentally, these challenges affect both human systems and the earth systems on which we depend. Planetary challenges include climate change, risks to oceans and forests, degradation to both biodiversity and material resources, and fundamental transformations of biogeochemical cycles. [2] Challenges facing society include widespread and intransigent environmental injustice, expanding urban and agricultural pollution, technological and economic lock-in of infrastructure and all manner of production and consumption systems, and a global dependence on carbon intensive energy. [2] The minor prioritizes integrative, interdisciplinary learning that is critical for effectively understanding and addressing the complexities of environmental issues today and in the future, and is structured on four pillars: Earth Systems and Climate Science, Environmental Governance, Environmental Histories and Cultures, and Engineering for Sustainability. [2] Upon completion of the minor, students will have achieved learning outcomes in seven categories: Systems Thinking; Sustainable Design Skills; Applied Sustainable Solutions; Know Your Planet; Social Context; Ethical Decision-making; and Impactful Communication. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Environmental Engineering Science
Requirements: The Minor in Environmental Engineering Science is offered by the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) for currently enrolled MIT undergraduates. The requirements consist of successfully completing a specific set of subjects. The minor also includes a fieldwork requirement through the Traveling Research Environmental Experiences (TREX) program during the Independent Activities Period (IAP). [2] To declare the minor, students must meet with a minor advisor, plan their program of study, and complete an application form, which should be accompanied by a copy of their unofficial transcript.

ProgramName: Minor in Finance
Requirements: To declare the Minor in Finance, students must fill out the Minor Application form and bring it with an unofficial transcript to room E52-154. [8] The requirements for completion consist of 5 subjects. [6] These include 3 Required Subjects (Managerial Finance: 15.417 or 15.401; Corporate Finance: 15.418 or 15.402; and Accounting: 15.501) and two elective subjects from an approved list. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in French
Requirements: To declare a minor, students consult with the appropriate minor advisor to develop a course plan and then submit a completed HASS Minor Application Form to the Global Languages Academic Program Specialist. [9] The minor consists of six subjects, commencing at semester III of the language curriculum. [9]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences (SHASS)
AverageScholarshipAmount: The median need-based MIT Scholarship was $69,777 for 2024–2025. [10]
ScholarshipAmount: A First-Year Grant of $2,000 is available for low-income first-year students. [10] Beginning with the 2025–2026 academic year, students whose family income is under $200,000 a year (with typical assets) attend MIT tuition-free. [8]

ProgramName: Minor in German
Requirements: The Minor in German consists of six subjects arranged into three levels of study. Depending on the student's entering competence, they may place out of the initial subjects. For students starting at a higher level, the six total subjects must be taken from the upper tiers in consultation with the minor advisor. [12, 16]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences. [9]
Description:
The minor in German provides students with a high level of proficiency in the German language and a solid knowledge of the culture in German-speaking countries. All subjects are taught by faculty in Global Languages, which is part of the School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences. The normal program for a minor includes the following:

Four subjects, including at least one of the following: 21G.403, 21G.404, 21G.410, or another advanced-level subject taught in German.
At least three of the four subjects must be taught in German.
No more than one subject may be taken with the Pass/D/Fail grading option.
Courses taken abroad as part of an MIT-approved program may be substituted for part of the minor program with prior approval from the German minor advisor.

ProgramName: Minor in History
Requirements: The Minor in History consists of six subjects, which must include: 21H.390 Theories and Methods in the Study of History, at least one 21H seminar (excluding 21H.390), and four additional subjects from the history curriculum. [9, 10] Of the five subjects other than 21H.390, at least two temporal periods—one pre-modern (before 1700) and one modern—must be covered. [1, 9, 10]
Description: The history minor provides students an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of the human past. Through coursework and a research paper, history minors learn how to pose historical questions, how to build answers by analyzing historical evidence in context, how to evaluate existing interpretations of the past, and how to write persuasively and elegantly. The department's courses explore a wide variety of regions, themes, and periods. They address questions about the transformation of societies over time and the diversity of human experience, through the study of politics and conflict, religion, race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality, or the production of knowledge (among many themes).

ProgramName: Minor in History of Architecture, Art, and Design
Minor in International Development
Requirements: The HASS Minor in International Development aims to increase students' ability to understand, analyze, and tackle problems of global poverty and economic development in the developing world. [7, 8, 9] The six-subject minor is structured into two tiers. [7, 8, 9] The subjects in the first tier provide a general overview of the history of international development, major theories and debates in the field, and an introduction to the dilemmas of practice. [7, 8, 9] The minor is offered by the Department of Urban Studies and Planning (DUSP). [7, 8, 9]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences (SHASS)
ScholarshipType: Need-based scholarships and grants from university, federal, and state sources. [12, 18]

ProgramName: Minor in Japanese
Requirements: To declare a minor in Japanese, students must consult with the appropriate minor advisor to develop a course plan and then submit a completed HASS Minor Application Form to the Global Languages Academic Program Specialist. [8] The minor generally consists of six subjects. [2] There is no mention of a competitive application process; it is a declaration for enrolled students.
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: Through the Global Languages program, students develop communicative and intercultural competencies, critical thinking skills, intellectual curiosity, diversity awareness, and cross-cultural understanding. [18] Japanese is presented as a Critical Language, as designated by the U.S. Department of State, due to Japan's close trading and political relationship with the U.S. and its role as a major exporter of culture. [23] The Japanese Studies curriculum at MIT is student-focused and uses online and technological tools, adapting innovative pedagogical methods to help students improve listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. [23] The program also offers a variety of cultural courses in areas like popular culture, anime, music, history, and politics to foster cultural fluency. [23] The study of the Japanese language is treated as a tool for interaction and communication, which must happen alongside cultural learning. [23]

ProgramName: Minor inJudaic Studies
Requirements: To declare a minor, students should complete an application form in consultation with the appropriate minor advisor. This should be done by the end of the sophomore year, but no later than Add Date one full term before the student's final term. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Latin American and Latino/a Studies
Requirements: The Minor in Latin American and Latino/a Studies consists of six subjects, with at least three being MIT subjects, including the required subject 17.55[J] Introduction to Latin American Studies. [9] These subjects are organized into four areas: Language (Area I), Humanities and the Arts (Area II), Social Sciences (Area III), and Historical Studies (Area IV). [9] Students can also take relevant subjects from Harvard University and Wellesley College through cross-registration with prior permission from the minor advisor. [9] Of the six subjects for the minor, a minimum of four cannot be applied toward a major or another minor. [9]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Concentration: ['Area I: Language', 'Area II: Humanities and the Arts', 'Area III: Social Sciences', 'Area IV: Historical Studies']
Description: An interdisciplinary minor that provides students with a foundational understanding of the languages, cultures, and societies of Latin America and the Latino/a diaspora in the United States. [1] The program is designed to be both international and comparative, acknowledging the diverse cultural experiences within Latin America and the U.S. Latino/a community. [1] The curriculum is structured around four areas of study: Language, Humanities and the Arts, Social Sciences, and Historical Studies. [1] Students are required to complete six subjects, with at least three being MIT subjects, including the mandatory course 17.55[J] Introduction to Latin American Studies. [1] The program also allows for cross-registration for relevant courses at Harvard University and Wellesley College, with prior approval from a minor advisor. [1] Five of the six subjects for the minor can be applied towards the eight-subject HASS Requirement. [1] At least four of the six subjects cannot be counted towards a major or another minor. [1]

ProgramName: Minor in Linguistics
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: The Minor in Linguistics consists of six subjects arranged in three levels of study, intended to provide students with breadth in the field of theoretical linguistics as a whole. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Literature
Requirements: Information regarding a formal application process, including a general description of requirements, is not available on the official Massachusetts Institute of Technology website for the Minor in Literature. The process typically involves fulfilling course requirements as an enrolled student.
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Concentration: ['Literature Focus', 'Film Focus']
Description: The Literature Section's mission is to maintain a level of excellence and innovation consistent with the best universities while remaining responsive to MIT's distinctive intellectual environment. The curriculum emphasizes interdisciplinary approaches to literary texts as well as theoretical, generic, and thematic subjects that range across geographical and historical boundaries. The minor aims to lay a foundation for advanced study and to enhance a student's appreciation of major narrative, poetic, and dramatic texts in relation to the cultures that produced them. [9] The program develops transferable skills in writing, comprehension, and analysis relevant to a variety of different professional paths—from journalism, law, and a variety of different professional paths—from journalism, law, and medical school to work in the gourmet food industry or computer game design. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Management
Requirements: To apply for the Minor in Management, current MIT students must fill out the 'Application for the Minors' form provided by the MIT Sloan School of Management. This form requires the student's name, MIT ID, email, current major(s), and expected degree award date. The completed form, along with an unofficial transcript, must be brought to the designated office (room E52-154, Suite 133). [6] The minor itself consists of completing six subjects. [8]
Description: The Minor in Management provides undergraduates in other majors with an understanding of the business, human, and organizational dimensions of scientific and technological enterprise. [4] The minor consists of six subjects.

ProgramName: Minor in Management Science
Description: A comprehensive description for the 'Minor in Management Science' is not available on the official Massachusetts Institute of Technology website. An application form indicates this minor was available for the classes of 2017 and 2018 only, suggesting it is no longer an active program under this name. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: The process to declare a Minor in Materials Science and Engineering is for current MIT students. The student must meet with the minor advisor in the chosen field to plan a program of study and complete an application form. A copy of the student's unofficial transcript should be brought to the meeting. [7] The academic requirement for the minor consists of completing six subjects: two required subjects (3.010 and 3.020), a choice of two core subjects, and two restricted electives. [8]
Description: The Department of Materials Science and Engineering (DMSE) offers a minor in Materials Science and Engineering. To be admitted, students must complete a minor application form, and obtain approval from the departmental undergraduate faculty advisor. The program requires six subjects, including two core subjects and four electives, each with a minimum of 9 units. The subjects must be completed with a grade of C or better and cannot be taken on a listener basis. A student may not use any subject as part of their minor program that has been used to satisfy their major program requirements. The minor is not available to students in Course 3.

ProgramName: Minor in Mathematics
Requirements: A Minor in Mathematics requires six 12-unit subjects in Course 18 (Mathematics). These six subjects must include: at least two subjects numbered 18.100 or higher; and at least two additional 'advanced subjects' (subjects whose first decimal digit is one or higher). Subjects offered jointly with another department count as subjects in Course 18. Other subjects outside Course 18 are not acceptable, even if they have strong mathematical content.
Description: A Minor in Mathematics requires six 12-unit subjects in Course 18. These six subjects must include: Subjects offered jointly with another department (e.g., 18.400J/6.1400J) count as subjects in Course 18. Other subjects outside Course 18 are not acceptable, even if they have strong mathematical content. There is no separate minor in Course 18C. [8]

ProgramName: Minor in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: To earn a minor in mechanical engineering, students must complete six 12-unit subjects from the Course 2 or 2-OE degree programs. Four of these subjects must be from the core curriculum of Course 2 or 2-OE (which can include 18.03). The remaining two subjects can be from the core curriculum or an elective in Course 2. It is noted that 6-unit subjects within the 2-A major are not eligible for the minor. [2]
Description: Students pursuing a minor in the department must complete a total of six 12-unit subjects drawn from the Course 2 or 2-OE degree programs. [1] Four of the six subjects must be from the Course 2 or 2-OE core curriculum (can include 18.03). [1] The last two subjects can either be from the core curriculum or can be an elective within Course 2. [1] The 6-unit subjects within the 2-A major do not qualify for the minor. [1]

ProgramName: Minor in Medical Anthropology
Requirements: The Minor in Anthropology consists of six subjects arranged into two tiers. Students create individual programs with the help of the minor advisor to ensure they gain a coherent understanding of the methods, approaches, and some of the results of the discipline. [10]

ProgramName: Minor in Middle Eastern Studies
Requirements: The minor consists of six subjects, with at least three being MIT subjects. The requirements are arranged in four areas of study: Area I: Language (two intermediate subjects in a Middle Eastern language), Area II: Humanities and the Arts, Area III: Social Sciences, and Area IV: Historical Studies. [1, 7] To declare the minor, students must meet with the minor advisor to plan their program of study and complete an application. [6]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description:
The goal of the HASS Minor Program in Middle Eastern Studies is to lead the student from the basic language into survey subjects and then into more focused studies of individual countries or specific historical periods, and to encourage analysis of the main methodological and conceptual issues in Middle Eastern Studies. The minor consists of six subjects (at least three of which must be MIT subjects), arranged in four areas of study: Area I: Language; Area II: Humanities and the Arts; Area III: Social Sciences; and Area IV: Historical Studies. [5]

Middle Eastern Studies at MIT offers students the opportunity to explore the connections among culture, society, politics, economics, technology, and environment in the Middle East, including North Africa. [5] MIT offers a number of subjects open to undergraduates that provide a variety of perspectives on the ancient, Islamic, and modern Middle East. [5]
ScholarshipAmount: The median MIT Scholarship was $69,777 for 2024–2025.

ProgramName: Minor in Music
Requirements: The Minor in Music requires six subjects that will give students experience within the three main branches of music: history/culture, composition/theory, and performance. [9]
Description: The Minor in Music requires six subjects that will give students experience within the three main branches of music: history/culture, composition/theory, and performance. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Nuclear Science and Engineering
Requirements: This minor allows students from any major outside of Course 22 to delve deeper into advanced topics within the department or to support interdisciplinary areas of interest in nuclear science and engineering. [1]
Description: This minor allows students from any major outside of Course 22 to delve deeper into advanced topics within the department or to support interdisciplinary areas of interest in nuclear science and engineering. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Philosophy
Requirements: For a minor in the field of philosophy, students must complete six philosophy subjects. These include: an introductory philosophy subject (numbered 24.00-24.09) or an appropriate Philosophy Concourse subject; a logic course (such as 24.118, 24.241, 24.242, 24.243, 24.244, 24.245, or an approved logic course from another department); three non-introductory philosophy subjects approved by the minor advisor; and 24.260, Topics in Philosophy. [10] At MIT, students apply to the university as a whole and are admitted as undeclared. They can later choose a minor without additional admission procedures or requirements. [5]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: The goal of the Minor in Philosophy is to introduce students to the methods of analytic philosophy and then to have them study a broad range of philosophers and philosophical issues at a more sophisticated level, culminating in an advanced seminar.

ProgramName: Minor in Physics
Requirements: The requirements for a minor in Physics are: 18.03 or 18.034, plus at least five Course 8 (Physics) subjects beyond the General Institute Requirements that constitute at least 57 units. [5, 6] To add the minor, a student must submit a completed Minor Application Form to the Physics Assistant Director with the permission of their academic advisor. [5] A Minor Completion Form must also be submitted when the classes are completed. [5]
Description: The Minor in Physics provides a solid foundation for the pursuit of a broad range of professional activities in science and engineering. The requirements for a minor in Physics are: 18.03 or 18.034, plus; at least five Course 8 subjects beyond the General Institute Requirements that constitute at least 57 units. [1]

ProgramName: Minor in Political Science
Requirements: A Minor in Political Science consists of six subjects. At least one but no more than two introductory subjects (Tier I), and at least four but no more than five upper-level subjects (Tier II). [1]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: A Minor in Political Science consists of six subjects (at least three of which must be MIT subjects) arranged in two tiers of study, Tier I and Tier II. No more than two subjects used to fulfill the requirements of the minor may also be counted toward a major or any other minor. Subjects taken under the junior-year GIR may not be used for the minor. All subjects for the minor must be taken for a letter grade and completed with a grade of C or better. For more information, contact the minor advisor, who can approve a student's minor program and sign the minor completion form.

ProgramName: Minor in Polymer Science and Engineering
Requirements: A minor in polymers and soft matter (MPSM) is an undergraduate minor program that consists of a minimum of six subjects or five subjects and a one-semester laboratory experience. Five of the subjects are core subjects in Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Engineering, and Ethics. Only one subject taken for the Minor in Polymers and Soft Matter can also count toward a student's major or another minor.
Description: The Minor in Polymers and Soft Matter is designed to equip students with the basic knowledge of polymer science and engineering required to solve problems in this diverse and essential field. [5] Students pursuing the minor complete four foundational subjects focusing on organic chemistry, polymer physics, and polymer engineering; a half-subject (6 units) on the basics of ethical guidelines for research; and one elective subject or approved UROP experience. [5] Only one subject taken for the Minor in Polymers and Soft Matter can also count toward a student's major or another minor. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Public Policy
Requirements: To declare the Minor in Public Policy, a student must meet with the public policy minor advisor to plan their program of study and fill out an application form. [7, 12] This should be done by the end of the sophomore year, but no later than Add Date one full term before the term in which the student's degree is awarded. [6] Urban Studies majors are not permitted to minor in Public Policy. [12]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences (SHASS)
Concentration: ['Social and Educational Policy', 'Energy and Environmental Policy', 'Infrastructure Policy', 'Science and Technology Policy', 'Labor and Industrial Policy', 'International Development Policy', 'Security and Defense Policy', 'Urban and Regional Policy', 'Health Policy']
Description: MIT's interdisciplinary Public Policy minor enables students from across the Institute to develop their understanding of public problems and how governments attempt to address them, with emphasis on the process and outcomes of policymaking. [5] The minor is a three-tiered program. The first tier provides foundational knowledge of public and private institutions where policy decisions are made and implemented, and an introduction to the rationales for government action and the policymaking process. [5] The second tier explores methods (both qualitative and quantitative) of analyzing and assessing the impacts of policy change. In the third tier, students choose an in-depth, three-subject program of study in a substantive field of policymaking. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Russian and Eurasian Studies
Requirements: The Minor in Russian and Eurasian Studies is intended for students seeking an interdisciplinary a program of study centered on Russia and Eurasia. The minor consists of six subjects (at least three of which must be MIT subjects or subjects taken at Harvard University or Wellesley College through cross-registration), arranged in four areas of study: Area I: Language; Area II: Humanities and the Arts; Area III: Social Sciences; and Area IV: Historical Studies. [3]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: The Minor in Russian and Eurasian Studies is intended for students seeking an interdisciplinary prog. [1]ram of study centered on Russia and Eurasia. [1] The program is regional in spirit, meaning that students can take subjects about a wide range of countries of Eastern/Central Europe, the Slavic states, and Central Asia. [1] The minor consists of six subjects (at least three of which must be MIT subjects or subjects taken at Harvard University or Wellesley College through cross-registration), arranged in four areas of study: Area I: Language; Area II: Humanities and the Arts; Area III: Social Sciences; Area IV: Historical Studies. [1]

ProgramName: Minor in Science, Technology, and Society
Requirements: The Minor in Science, Technology, and Society is for current MIT students. The process involves completing a HASS Minor Application Form in consultation with the appropriate minor advisor. [3, 6] Students should apply for the minor no later than Add Date one full term before the term in which the degree is awarded. [3] The coursework for the minor consists of six subjects, including at least one Tier I subject, one Tier II subject, and STS.004. [7]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
Description: The goal of the minor program in Science, Technology, and Society (STS) is to provide students with a broad social perspective on the fields of engineering and science, including how they have evolved and how they fit into the wider context of society, culture, politics, and values. [3, 4] The minor is designed to be a complement to technical fields and may be of particular interest to students majoring in the natural sciences or enrolled in the School of Engineering. [2] The minor consists of six subjects, which must include at least two courses with a 'Core' designation, one Reading Lab, and at least one semester of the Lunch Seminar, for a total of at least 18 credits. [2] All six courses must be graded C- or higher and cannot be taken on a Pass/Fail basis. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Scientific and Engineering Communication
Requirements: The minor consists of six subjects. A student must complete two tiers of study. Tier I requires one subject from a specified list of writing and rhetoric courses. Tier II requires five additional subjects, with at least four from the Program in Writing, and allows up to two of these to be drawn from a list of approved subjects in other HASS fields. [3]
Fees: $61,990 per year for tuition for the 2024-2025 academic year. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Spanish
Requirements: A minor in Spanish at MIT is part of the School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences. To declare a minor, students do not have additional application requirements as they apply to the entire university and not a specific program. First-year students at MIT are undeclared and receive guidance to choose their major and minor.
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Statistics and Data Science
Requirements: The Minor in Statistics and Data Science is available to MIT undergraduates from any major. [2] To apply, the student must complete an application form for the minor in consultation with an appropriate minor advisor. [8] The program requires the completion of seven subjects, including foundational courses, two statistics subjects, two computation and data analysis subjects, and a capstone subject. [7] A minimum of four subjects taken for the Statistics and Data Science Minor cannot also count toward a major or another minor. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Theater Arts
Requirements: To apply for the Minor in Theater Arts, a student must be a current MIT undergraduate. The process involves filling out the 'HASS Minor Application Form' in consultation with the Theater Arts minor advisor. [9, 10] This form documents the student's planned program of study to meet the minor's course requirements. The requirements for completing the minor are choosing one course from a core group of foundational classes and five elective courses for a total of at least 69 units. [3] The application form should preferably be submitted by the end of the student's junior year. [9]
Description: The Minor in Theater Arts is designed to give students the opportunity to experiment in the making of theater. [2] The flexibility of the minor allows students either to explore the basic principles of several theater disciplines or to concentrate more deeply on one. [2] In conjunction with the minor advisor, students select a coherent program of Theater Arts subjects. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Toxicology and Environmental Health
Requirements: The program consists of three required didactic core subjects and one laboratory subject, as well as one restricted elective. The prerequisites for the core subjects are 5.111 /5.112 Principles of Chemical Science or 3.091 Introduction to Solid-State Chemistry plus Introductory Biology (7.012 / 7.013 / 7.014 / 7.015 / 7.016). [2]
Description: The Department of Biological Engineering offers an undergraduate Minor in Toxicology and Environmental Health. The goal of this program is to meet the growing demand for undergraduates to acquire the intellectual tools needed to understand and assess the impact of new products and processes on human health, and to provide a perspective on the risks of human exposure to synthetic and natural chemicals, physical agents, and microorganisms. [13] Given the importance of environmental education at MIT, the program is designed to be accessible to any MIT undergraduate. [13]

ProgramName: Minor in Urban Studies and Planning
Requirements: The six-subject Minor in Urban Studies and Planning is available to all MIT undergraduates. To complete the minor, students must take two Tier I subjects that establish the political, economic, and design contexts for decision-making, and four Tier II elective subjects. Students are encouraged to consult with the minor advisor to craft a program that reflects their interests.

ProgramName: Minor in Women's and Gender Studies
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Minor in Writing
Requirements: To declare a Minor in Writing, a current MIT student must meet with the minor advisor in the field to plan a program of study, which consists of five to seven subjects. The student must then complete and submit the HASS Minor Application Form. [6, 8, 13]
Department: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
